papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: To understand and improve long-term congenital heart surgery outcomes, longitudinal data are essential but challenging to capture. We evaluated a novel program to facilitate routine longitudinal data collection. METHODS: Patients undergoing Society of Thoracic Surgeons Benchmark Operations at two centers (2007-2019) were included. Annual follow-up data (vital status and age-specific burden of disease questionnaires) were collected using an automated email system along with medical record and local registry data queries, with coordinator follow-up if needed. Completeness of follow-up and associated factors were analyzed in multivariable logistic regression. RESULTS: Of 4,075 subjects, vital status was captured for 98% (median follow-up 6.0 years; IQR 3.1-9.2). Vital status at one year was known for 95%; overall follow-up completeness (observed-to-potential follow-up time) was 81%. At least one follow-up questionnaire was completed by 85%, with 58% utilizing the automated email system. Those with genetic/non-cardiac abnormalities (OR 2.28, 95%CI 1.28-4.28), single ventricle palliation (Norwood OR 11.2, 95%CI 3.01-72.7; Glenn/hemi-Fontan OR 7.79, 95%CI 2.21-49.5), and tetralogy of Fallot repair (OR 2.43, 95%CI 1.11-5.59) had higher odds of known vital status. Follow-up questionnaire completion had higher odds for non-Hispanic white patients (OR 1.54, 95%CI: 1.27-1.86) and higher median income households (OR 1.05/$10,000, 95%CI: 1.01-1.09). CONCLUSIONS: This program captured vital status and burden of disease, with one-year survival determined for nearly all patients. Automation reduced human resource needs by more than half. Future efforts will focus on expanding to other centers and improving follow-up for disadvantaged groups.

papers.abstract_full: Hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS) is a complex congenital heart disease (CHD) involving hypoplasia of the left ventricle (LV) and the aorta (Ao), along with aortic and mitral valve stenosis/atresia with or without coarctation. It is a physiologically single-ventricle lesion, previously uniformly fatal, but now survivable with a 3-stage surgical palliation ending with the Fontan circulation, a circulation for only one working ventricle. In the classical definition of HLHS, the ventricular septum is intact; however, HLHS variants have been described with similar single-ventricle pathophysiology in which the hypoplastic LV is not hemodynamically coupled to the aortic outflow. Evidence for a genetic etiology for HLHS is indicated by its high recurrence risk, the association with various chromosomal abnormalities, and the demonstration of mutations in mice causing HLHS. Despite surgical advances allowing survival of patients with HLHS, there is still high morbidity and mortality after their first-stage palliation. The causes of such high morbidity and mortality are not well understood, but most deaths are likely related to cardiovascular/hemodynamic causes. Studies in the animal models of HLHS show that this cardiac lesion arises early in embryogenesis, decreases left-sided inflow, and is associated with metabolic dysfunction, cell proliferation, and differentiation defects. Findings indicate HLHS is also associated with intrinsic cell deficits, deficits that may also contribute to the high risk of heart failure and adverse neurodevelopment. In this article, we update a previous review by describing the basic pathophysiology; pertinent pre- and postoperative management of HLHS and its anatomical variants; and novel insights from the HLHS mouse model on the causes of HLHS-associated heart failure and poor neurodevelopment, as well as potential therapeutic strategies.

papers.abstract_full: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) is characterized by progressive ventricular dilation, systolic dysfunction, and an increased risk of arrythmias and sudden cardiac arrest. Variants in the LMNA gene, which encodes the nuclear lamins A and C, have been linked to the familial form of the disease and the founder variant p.Ser143Pro is particularly common among Finnish patients with DCM. To elucidate the complex and poorly understood pathogenic mechanisms behind LMNA-related DCM, we generated a mouse model carrying the p.Ser143Pro mutation in the Lmna gene. All genetically modified mice appeared normal at birth. However, based on echocardiography, necropsy, natriuretic peptide B (Nppb) expression levels, and histopathological data, homozygous males developed progressive left ventricular dilatation, myocardial fibrosis, and cardiac failure after 6 months of age, with all succumbing before 10 months. A reduced disease penetrance was observed in heterozygous male and homozygous female mice, with one-year survival rates of 40% and 60%, respectively. No signs of skeletal myopathy were observed in mice carrying the mutation. Whole-transcriptome RNA sequencing analysis of left ventricular cardiac tissue from asymptomatic two-month-old homozygous male mice revealed an upregulation of classical heart failure markers, such as natriuretic peptide A (Nppa) and myosin heavy chain 7 (Myh7), and an elevated unfolded protein response signaling, as shown by elevated DNA damage inducible transcript 3 (Ddit3), BAG cochaperone 3 (Bag3) and CCAAT enhancer binding protein beta (Cebpb) levels. In conclusion, p.Ser143Pro-Lmna mice closely mimic the clinical phenotype observed in patients with the p.Ser143Pro LMNA variant and offer a valuable in vivo model for investigating the underlying pathogenic mechanisms of LMNA-related DCM. © 2026 The Author(s). papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) is genetically heterogeneous. In severe non-ischemic DCM with familial clustering of heart-failure deaths, genetic testing and pedigree analysis may clarify etiology and guide cascade screening. CASE PRESENTATION: A 40-year-old woman presented with progressive dyspnea, chest tightness, and palpitations after an upper respiratory tract infection. Echocardiography showed severe left ventricular systolic dysfunction [left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) approximately 20%], left atrial enlargement, functional mitral regurgitation, and a small pericardial effusion. Serial cardiac troponin I and myocardial enzyme measurements remained within the reference ranges. Coronary angiography excluded obstructive coronary disease. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) demonstrated global left ventricular hypokinesis and a clinically reported non-ischemic late-gadolinium-enhancement pattern at the papillary-muscle level involving the anterior/lateral wall. Because cardiac biomarkers remained normal and dedicated inflammatory CMR sequences were not acquired, active myocarditis could not be confirmed. Guideline-directed therapy reduced NT-proBNP from 4154 to 828 pg/mL, although angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor therapy was limited by symptomatic hypotension. At 2 months, symptoms and daily activity tolerance improved, but LVEF remained 25%, QTc was 479 ms, and ventricular premature complexes persisted. Whole-exome sequencing identified heterozygous likely pathogenic variants in BAG3 (NM_004281.4:c.180 + 1G > T) and FLNC [NM_001458.5:c.761_779del, p.(Leu254Profs*14)]. The daughter carried the BAG3 variant, whereas both children were negative for FLNC. The proband reported heart-failure-related deaths in her father and younger brother during adulthood and in a nephew during childhood. CONCLUSIONS: The findings support complex familial non-ischemic DCM with marked variable expressivity. Coexisting BAG3 and FLNC variants should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating rather than proof of dual-gene causality. The infection-associated acute decompensation, persistently normal cardiac injury biomarkers, non-ischemic LGE, and incomplete inflammatory CMR characterization favor cautious interpretation rather than a definitive diagnosis of myocarditis. Serial imaging, rhythm surveillance, individualized device-risk assessment, and follow-up of genotype-positive relatives are essential.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: A major challenge in dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) care is the identification and management of individuals at risk before disease manifestation. An artificial intelligence (AI) model applied to electrocardiography (ECG) was developed to detect and predict the echocardiographic DCM phenotype (left ventricular dilatation with systolic dysfunction) and was evaluated for its ability to stratify the risk of incident DCM in familial cohorts. METHODS: A deep learning model was trained to detect the echocardiographic DCM phenotype and to predict its future onset, using more than 330 000 ECG-echocardiogram pairs from the Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, Boston. Model performance was validated in cohorts from the UK Biobank, Zhongshan Hospital, and Antwerp University Hospital, and compared with models based on traditional ECG features and echocardiographic traits. To assess performance in familial DCM, genetically predisposed individuals identified through cascade screening at the cardiogenetics clinics of Antwerp University Hospital (n = 166, 18% DCM positive) and Maastricht University Medical Center (n = 177, 18% DCM positive) were evaluated. RESULTS: The AI-ECG model achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of .87-.97 for diagnosing the prevalent DCM phenotype, outperforming traditional ECG parameters. AI-ECG was comparable to echocardiography for predicting future DCM (C-index .80-.87 and .80-.90, respectively). In familial cohorts, 5-year negative predictive values were 95.5% (Antwerp) and 91.5% (Maastricht), with corresponding positive predictive values of 42.4% and 39.4%, while high-risk scores were associated with a 5.1-6.4-fold increased risk of incident DCM. CONCLUSIONS: The explainable AI-ECG model detects the echocardiographic DCM phenotype and predicts future disease, and supports the exclusion of short- to mid-term disease in genetically at-risk individuals. This low-cost tool could help reduce surveillance burden and facilitate earlier intervention.

papers.abstract_full: Summary  Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) is a severe heart condition often linked to arrhythmias, clots, and heart failure, for which treatments are not yet curative. Recently,  de novo mutations in genes encoding components of the Rag GTPase nutrient signaling pathway, particularly in  RRAGC , have been found in unrelated patients with a severe, early-onset DCM syndrome called Long-Olsen-Distelmaier. Cancer cell lines, hiPSC-derived cardiomyocytes and zebrafish have been used to study this  Ragopathy , but a mammalian model to investigate this syndrome has not been generated. Here, we show that mice engineered to endogenously express mutations in Serine 74 (orthologous to the Serine 75 mutated in patients), exhibit early-onset features of DCM with decreased heart size, fibrosis, diastolic dysfunction and aortic insufficiency, characteristics reminiscent of the human syndrome. Moreover,  Rragc -mutant hearts display decreased left ventricular mass and interventricular septum. Endogenous heterozygous expression of  Rragc mutant variants result in a milder, sublethal defective physiological cardiac growth with increased systolic and diastolic blood pressure. Mechanistically, active RagC does not cause abnormal increase in cardiomyocyte size, but leads to suppressed transcriptional activity of Tfeb and alterations in cardiomyocyte metabolism. Transcriptional profiling of neonatal mutant hearts reveals multiple signatures of impaired mitochondrial activity.  Ex vivo and  in vitro analyses of murine cardiomyocyte mitochondria from  Rragc -mutant mice show suppressed mitochondrial respiration, disturbed complex IV multimerization and super-complex organization. These data point to abnormal early postnatal heart metabolism by deregulated nutrient – Rag GTPase signaling with a potential molecular explanation to the early onset of DCM in patients with  de novo missense mutations in  RRAGC , and suggests the relevance of early metabolic interventions in conditions with altered nutrient signaling.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) is a genetic disorder impairing mucociliary clearance. This study provides a comprehensive analysis of clinical and genetic characteristics in a large Turkish cohort with frequent parental consanguinity. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was performed on 145 patients (selected from 361) with regular follow-up since 2017 to ensure longitudinal data consistency. The diagnostic work-up included nasal nitric oxide measurement and high-speed videomicroscopy, while confirmation was established through genetic testing and/or transmission electron microscopy. Patients were classified according to the 2025 ATS/ERS diagnostic framework. Patients were evaluated for clinical predictors, longitudinal pulmonary function, and genotype-phenotype correlations based on structural protein localization. RESULTS: Among 145 patients (mean age 15.91 ± 6.26 years), early diagnosis was significantly associated with neonatal respiratory distress syndrome (p = 0.014), NICU admission (p < 0.001), situs inversus totalis (p < 0.001), and congenital heart disease (p < 0.001). The mean PICADAR score was 7.8 ± 3.4, showing a moderate negative correlation with age at diagnosis (r = -0.50, p < 0.001). According to the 2025 ATS/ERS diagnostic framework, 63 patients (43.4%) were classified as confirmed PCD, 13 (9.0%) as PCD highly likely, and 69 (47.6%) as suspected PCD. Among confirmed PCD patients, the most frequent genetic findings were DNAH5, CCDC40, and DNAAF1. Lower final FEV1 values were observed in selected rare genotype subgroups, particularly CCNO, although variant-specific comparisons were limited by small subgroup sizes. CONCLUSION: Early recognition of neonatal respiratory distress requiring NICU admission and laterality defects, particularly situs inversus totalis, remains critical for reducing diagnostic delay. In populations with high consanguinity, genetic testing is particularly important for confirming diagnosis and identifying potentially high-risk genotypes. Multidisciplinary follow-up focusing on nutrition, infection control, and preservation of lung function is essential for long-term care in PCD.

papers.abstract_full: INTRODUCTION: Situs inversus is a rare congenital condition characterized by a mirror-image reversal of thoracic and/or abdominal organs, with an estimated incidence of 1 in 10,000 live births. Although many individuals are asymptomatic, the condition is associated with congenital heart disease (CHD), and because a mirror-image heart may appear structurally normal, it can be overlooked at routine prenatal ultrasonography unless fetal laterality is determined first. CASE DESCRIPTION: A 25-year-old primigravida was referred at 34-35 weeks of gestation for evaluation of fetal growth restriction; fetal situs inversus had not been identified at previous antenatal examinations. Ultrasonography showed the stomach on the right, the liver on the left, the descending aorta to the right of the spine and the inferior vena cava to the left, with the cardiac apex directed to the right. Fetal echocardiography confirmed atrial situs inversus with mirror-image dextrocardia and normal systemic and pulmonary venous return, without structural cardiac defects or features of heterotaxy. Doppler indices were normal, and the fetus was categorized as small for gestational age. The patient delivered a neonate weighing 2365 grams vaginally at 39 weeks and 4 days, and postnatal echocardiography confirmed mirror-image dextrocardia with normal intracardiac anatomy. CONCLUSION: Isolated situs inversus totalis can remain undetected until the third trimester because each standard view of a mirror-image heart appears normal. Determining fetal laterality at the start of every obstetric scan, followed by detailed fetal echocardiography to exclude CHD and heterotaxy, consideration of genetic evaluation, and postnatal follow-up for primary ciliary dyskinesia, allows accurate counseling and appropriate perinatal planning.

papers.abstract_full: Ellis-Yale-Winter syndrome (EYWS) is an exceptionally rare multiple congenital anomaly syndrome characterized by microcephaly and congenital heart disease, variably associated with unilateral renal agenesis and abnormal pulmonary lobation. Its phenotype derives from a single original sibship, no validated diagnostic criteria exist, and no causative gene has been established. We report a male infant with congenital microcephaly, right renal agenesis with a contralateral ectopic solitary kidney, congenital heart defects, craniofacial dysmorphic features, and neurological abnormalities. The findings showed phenotypic overlap with the original cases, leading a multidisciplinary team to a suspected clinical diagnosis of EYWS. This diagnosis is not molecularly confirmed, as no genetic testing was performed. Pulmonary lobation and segmentation could not be assessed, which is a major limitation; their presence or absence cannot be inferred. The contralateral renal ectopia may represent a coincidental malformation or a hypothetical phenotypic variant. Long-term outcome and vital status are undetermined. This report does not establish new diagnostic features or an expanded phenotypic spectrum. Dedicated pulmonary imaging, exome or genome sequencing, DNA banking, and longitudinal follow-up are recommended in future cases.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Coffin-Lowry syndrome is a rare X-linked genetic disorder caused by pathogenic variants in the RPS6KA3 gene, characterized by distinctive craniofacial features, skeletal abnormalities, and neurodevelopmental impairment. Although cardiac involvement has been reported in Coffin-Lowry syndrome, it most commonly manifests as cardiomyopathy or valvular insufficiency. To the best of our knowledge, Coffin-Lowry syndrome has not been associated with obstructive left-sided congenital heart diseases including an incomplete Shone's complex. CASE PRESENTATION: We report a case of a 2-month-old boy who, on cardiac evaluation, was found to have coarctation of the aorta, a bicuspid aortic valve with severe stenosis, a parachute-like mitral valve with mild subvalvular stenosis, consistent with an incomplete Shone's complex, and marked left ventricular hypertrophy. The patient underwent successful corrective surgery for coarctation of the aorta and aortic valve stenosis, with follow-up revealing moderate residual aortic valve stenosis and mild residual valvular dysfunction. Genetic testing identified a maternally inherited microduplication of the X chromosome p22.12 region, encompassing several 5' exons of the RPS6KA3 gene. CONCLUSIONS: This case suggests that obstructive left-sided congenital heart diseases including an incomplete Shone's complex may represent a previously unrecognized cardiac manifestations of Coffin-Lowry syndrome, thereby expanding the cardiovascular phenotype of this rare condition. Recognition of this association may have implications for early diagnosis, genetic evaluation, and long-term cardiac surveillance in affected patients.

papers.abstract_full: INTRODUCTION: Ring chromosome 21 (r (21)) is a rare constitutional rearrangement involving terminal deletions and significant phenotypic heterogeneity. High-resolution genomic analyses have demonstrated that ring chromosomes may harbor complex genomic imbalances and dynamic mosaicism. However, the contributions of ring chromosome instability, tissue-specific mosaicism, and complex dosage imbalance to the clinical phenotype remain poorly understood. CASE PRESENTATION: We report an 8-month-old boy with developmental delay, congenital heart disease, hearing impairment, structural brain abnormalities, and dysmorphic features suggestive of Down syndrome (DS), although lacking the complete classical phenotype. Cytogenomic analyses identified a constitutional non-supernumerary r (21) associated with a 18.77-Mb duplication of 21q21.2-q22.3 and a 3.09-Mb terminal deletion of 21q22.3. Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) resolved the ring chromosome structure, identifying four instability-derived clones, and demonstrated tissue-specific mosaicism across lymphocytes, oral mucosa epithelial cells, and urinary sediment epithelial cells, with a duplicated monocentric r (21) as the predominant clone. Comparison with the four previously reported constitutional non-supernumerary r (21) cases revealed a recurrent combination of Down syndrome critical region (DSCR) duplication and terminal 21q deletion, despite substantial phenotypic variability. DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION: This study expands the clinical and cytogenomic spectrum associated with constitutional non-supernumerary r (21). Tissue-specific mosaicism and recurrent genomic imbalances suggest that the DS-like phenotype cannot be explained solely by dosage alterations involving the classical or highly restricted DSCR. Our findings suggest a mechanism in which dynamic ring chromosome instability, and the cumulative dosage imbalance of multiple chromos​ome 21 genes, contribute to the phenotypic variability observed in these patients. Additional well-characterized cases are essential for refining the genotype-phenotype correlations of this rare genomic disorder.

papers.abstract_full: Accurate assessment of patient knowledge is an essential component of informed decision-making in cardiac genetic testing. An eight-item cardiac genetic knowledge scale was previously developed to support evaluation of informed choice within the Multidimensional Model of Informed Choice, but its psychometric properties have not been formally assessed. Data were pooled from 318 adults with hypertrophic or dilated cardiomyopathy who received pretest education through a genetics webinar (n = 121), cardiologist-led counseling (n = 61), or a prerecorded educational video (n = 136). Exploratory factor analysis (EFA), confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), and two-parameter logistic item response theory (IRT) modeling were used to evaluate factor structure, item performance, and measurement precision. Mean knowledge scores ranged from 6.2 to 7.1 out of 8, with 62%-91% of participants classified as having adequate knowledge (≥ 75%). EFA supported a two-factor solution reflecting disease-related and testing-related knowledge; however, CFA demonstrated substantial overlap between these domains (r = 0.81), with one- and two-factor models showing comparable fit. Overall, findings supported a dominant general knowledge construct. IRT analyses demonstrated acceptable model fit (M2 = 39.35, df = 20, p = 0.006) and meaningful variability in item performance. Two items showed strong discrimination across the knowledge continuum, while several items contributed less information. All items had negative difficulty parameters, indicating that the scale was primarily targeted toward individuals with below-average knowledge. Test information curves showed greatest measurement precision at low-to-moderate knowledge levels. Raw scores were highly correlated with latent trait estimates (r = 0.97, p < 0.001), supporting the practicality of simple sum-score interpretation. This study provides preliminary evidence supporting the internal structural validity of the eight-item cardiac genetic knowledge scale. The scale demonstrated acceptable item performance in this sample and effectively identified individuals with lower levels of knowledge and specific educational gaps across care models, supporting its potential use as the knowledge component of informed decision-making measures in cardiac genetic testing.

papers.abstract_full: The role of RNA-binding proteins in metabolic gene regulation is unclear. Here, we uncover a hierarchical circuit where RNA-binding protein RBFOX2 establishes lipid gene programs and lipidome in embryonic hearts by governing transcription factors (TFs) using multi-transcriptomic and lipidomics approaches. We identified TF and lipid genes as RBFOX2 targets in the embryonic heart. TF SOX4 is a key target of RBFOX2 that drives lipid gene programs. RBFOX2 binds human SOX4 3' UTR and regulates its mRNA stability. SOX4 in turn initiates a lipid gene program by binding promoters of lipid enzymes/regulators. Restoration of SOX4 level, rescues lipid gene expression defects upon RBFOX2 loss. Strikingly, Rbfox2 loss in embryonic hearts modulates cardiac lipidome and leads to accumulation of lipid droplets. We reveal an RNA-mediated mechanism that establishes lipidome identity in the developing heart and may provide unique metabolic nodes vulnerable for pharmaceutic intervention of congenital heart disease in the future.

papers.abstract_full: INTRODUCTION: Maternal use of selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), including sertraline, has been associated with an increased risk of congenital heart defects, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. SSRIs cross the placenta and may influence cardiac development during sensitive periods. Previous work showed that perinatal sertraline exposure impairs postnatal growth, alters cardiomyocyte calcium handling, dysregulates serotonin signaling genes (Htr2a, Htr2b, and Slc6a4), and chronically reduces left ventricular size. We hypothesized that these effects may involve early epigenetic alterations in cardiac DNA methylation. MATERIALS & METHODS: Adult female C57BL/6J mice received daily intraperitoneal injections of sertraline (5 mg/kg) or saline for five days before mating and throughout gestation. Offspring continued to receive 1.5 mg/kg of sertraline until postnatal day 14 (PN14), when hearts were collected. Global DNA methylation (5-methylcytosine, 5-mC) was quantified using a colorimetric ELISA assay. Targeted bisulfite sequencing (TBS-seq) profiled CpG methylation across predefined promoter and regulatory regions of 10 genes involved in serotonin signaling and cardiac function. Regional differential methylation was analyzed across 23 regions using overdispersion-corrected logistic regression with Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) adjustment. RESULTS: Global 5-mC levels did not differ significantly between sertraline-exposed and control groups. TBS-seq identified 1,941 CpG sites across 25 targeted regions. After coverage and regional quality filtering, 1,411 CpG sites across 23 regions were retained. Regional analysis identified two regions with significant differential methylation after FDR correction: the Htr2a enhancer showed an 8.19% increase in methylation (p < 4.1 × 10-15, q < 9.4 × 10-14), whereas the Tph2-associated region showed a 3.00% decrease in sertraline-exposed animals (p < 0.0020, q < 0.0229). Secondary site-level analyses identified no individual CpG sites that remained significant after multiple-testing correction. Overall methylation profiles were highly correlated across samples, with no significant global difference between treatment groups. DISCUSSION: Perinatal sertraline exposure was associated with localized regional DNA methylation changes in neonatal cardiac tissue without a global change in 5-mC. The Htr2a enhancer and Tph2-associated region represent candidate regulatory loci linking early-life SSRI exposure with cardiac serotonergic pathways. These findings support further investigation of regional epigenetic alterations using integrated methylation, transcriptomic, and cell-type-resolved approaches to determine their functional significance and potential contribution to later-life cardiovascular outcomes.

papers.abstract_full: UNLABELLED: Arrhythmogenic left ventricular cardiomyopathy (ALVC) is an increasingly recognized phenotype within the spectrum of arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathies, historically associated with mutations in desmosomal genes. However, emerging evidence suggests that non-desmosomal variants may also contribute to this disease entity. We report the case of a 58-year-old man with atrial fibrillation, nonischemic cardiomyopathy, and prior cryptogenic stroke who presented with progressive exertional dyspnea, chest discomfort, and palpitations. Coronary angiography excluded obstructive coronary artery disease. Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated reduced left ventricular systolic function with features suggestive of infiltrative cardiomyopathy. A technetium-99m pyrophosphate scan was negative for transthyretin amyloidosis. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging ultimately revealed extensive mid-wall late gadolinium enhancement involving multiple basal and mid-left ventricular segments in a nonischemic distribution, consistent with myocardial fibrosis. Comprehensive genetic testing identified a heterozygous pathogenic MYH7 variant (p.Arg723Cys), fulfilling the genetic component of the Padua criteria for ALVC. Rhythm control was achieved with electrical cardioversion and maintained with dofetilide, while heart failure was managed with guideline-directed medical therapy. In view of the extensive myocardial fibrosis and reduced left ventricular ejection fraction, primary prevention with an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator was recommended. This case expands the phenotypic spectrum of MYH7-associated cardiomyopathy and highlights the critical role of multimodal imaging and genetic testing in establishing the diagnosis of ALVC and guiding risk stratification. CLINICAL IMPACT: Arrhythmogenic left ventricular cardiomyopathy (ALVC) remains an underrecognized and diagnostically challenging phenotype of arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy. This case describes a potential association between the pathogenic MYH7 p.Arg723Cys variant and ALVC, expanding the phenotypic spectrum of MYH7-associated cardiomyopathy beyond its more established associations with hypertrophic and dilated cardiomyopathy. The case highlights the complementary roles of cardiac magnetic resonance imaging and genetic testing in identifying ALVC when conventional evaluation is inconclusive. Recognition of extensive myocardial fibrosis together with a pathogenic genetic variant may also provide important information for arrhythmic risk stratification, consideration of primary-prevention implantable cardioverter-defibrillator therapy, genetic counseling, and cascade testing of first-degree relatives.

papers.abstract_full: LEMD2 is an inner nuclear membrane protein that interacts with LMNA and contributes to nuclear membrane integrity and chromatin organization. Pathogenic LEMD2 variants are associated with progressive cardiomyopathy, but the relationship between Lemd2 protein abundance and disease severity remains unclear. Using computational modeling, we designed a Lemd2 in-frame deletion (p.Glu8_Leu9del, ΔE8_L9) within the LEM domain, predicted to alter its conformation, and generated knock-in (KI) mouse by CRISPR/Cas9. Western blot analysis demonstrated that the ΔE8_L9 deletion was associated with a near-complete loss of Lemd2 protein. Findings were considered alongside those previously reported for the Lemd2 p.L13R KI model, which retains ~68% of Lemd2 protein, to describe the cardiac phenotype and nuclear phenotypes associated with two distinct LEM-domain mutations. ΔE8_L9 homozygous mice exhibited postnatal growth retardation and rapidly progressive dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) with systolic dysfunction and myocardial fibrosis by postnatal day 21 (P21), whereas the reported p.L13R model exhibited later-onset DCM. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) revealed dense intranuclear chromatin aggregates and peripheral heterochromatin accumulation in cardiomyocytes. Bulk RNA sequencing identified downregulation of DNA replication- and DNA repair-related pathways at P1.5 and upregulation of mechanical stress-, senescence-, and immune response-related pathways at P21. Consistently, ΔE8_L9 hearts exhibited increased γ-H2AX-positive DNA damage and a numerically lower percentage of Ki-67-positive cardiomyocytes. The ΔE8_L9 model is associated with marked Lemd2 protein reduction, nuclear membrane abnormalities, altered chromatin architecture, DNA damage, and early-onset DCM.

papers.abstract_full: Alcoholic cardiomyopathy (ACM) is a major form of non-ischaemic dilated cardiomyopathy characterized by ventricular dilation and impaired systolic function following chronic alcohol exposure. Despite partial reversibility with prolonged abstinence, ACM remains an important cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, while the molecular mechanisms driving disease initiation and progression are incompletely understood. Emerging evidence indicates that ACM is not solely a consequence of direct ethanol toxicity, but rather a complex disorder involving interconnected metabolic, inflammatory, immune, and epigenetic pathways. In this review, we summarize current advances in the pathophysiology of ACM and propose an integrated immunometabolic framework underlying disease progression. Chronic alcohol exposure induces oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, calcium mishandling, and endoplasmic reticulum stress, leading to cardiomyocyte injury and impaired cellular energetics. These disturbances activate pro-inflammatory signaling pathways, including NF-κB and the NLRP3 inflammasome, promoting cytokine production and inflammatory forms of programmed cell death such as pyroptosis. Concurrently, accumulating evidence implicates immune dysregulation as a central contributor to adverse remodeling, characterized by altered T-cell polarization, macrophage phenotypic switching, and dysregulated immune checkpoint signaling that sustain chronic inflammation and fibrosis. In parallel, alcohol-induced epigenetic and post-transcriptional mechanisms, including DNA methylation, histone modifications, and microRNA-mediated regulation, establish persistent transcriptional reprogramming that links transient metabolic stress to long-term alterations in cardiomyocyte function and myocardial structure. Collectively, these pathways form a self-reinforcing network of metabolic injury, immune activation, and maladaptive remodeling that drives ACM progression. A more integrated understanding of these mechanisms identifies oxidative stress, inflammasome activation, immune imbalance, and epigenetic reprogramming as interconnected and potentially targetable processes. Therapeutic strategies combining alcohol abstinence with mechanism-based interventions targeting these pathways may provide new opportunities for precision treatment of ACM.

papers.abstract_full: Pilomatricoma is a rare benign cutaneous neoplasm that may occur more frequently in syndromic conditions such as Turner syndrome (TS). This study aimed to evaluate the prevalence and clinical characteristics of pilomatricoma and its association with clinical factors, serum vitamin D (VD) levels, and genetic variants in the VD pathway in patients with TS. Clinical variables and serum VD levels were obtained from medical records, and single-nucleotide variants in the GC, NADSYN1, and VDR genes were analyzed by allelic discrimination using real-time polymerase chain reaction. Among 97 patients with TS, six cases of histopathologically confirmed pilomatricoma were identified, corresponding to a prevalence of 6.2%, with lesions predominantly located on the head and upper extremities. Four patients (66.7%) had renal malformations. In exploratory multivariable analysis, renal malformations were significantly associated with pilomatricoma (adjusted OR = 14.2; 95% CI: 2.1-95.4; nominal p = 0.008; FDR-adjusted p = 0.032). No significant associations were observed with serum VD levels or the analyzed genetic variants. These findings suggest that pilomatricoma may be more frequent in TS than previously reported and identify an exploratory association between pilomatricoma and renal malformations. Given the small number of pilomatricoma cases, this association requires confirmation in larger independent cohorts.

papers.abstract_full: Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy (ACM), a genetic heart muscle disease that affects primarily the right ventricle, can lead to sudden cardiac death. Although ACM was initially classified as a dysplasia due to a congenital abnormality in the growth of the right ventricle, it was later demonstrated to be caused by a genetic defect in the cardiac desmosomes. Mutations in genes that encode components of the desmosomes, that is, the adhesive junctions that connect cardiomyocytes, are the most common cause of ACMs. However, the specific molecular mechanisms that lead to myocardial destruction, remodeling, and arrhythmogenic predisposition are unclear. Recent advances in the understanding of the pathogenic mechanisms of ACM have focused on mechanisms including cardiomyocyte loss, fibrosis, and adipogenesis, which occur through different signaling pathways such as Wnt signaling, PPARγ signaling, and the Hippo-Yes-associated protein pathway. Inflammation also plays a role in the development of ACM. Regarding the diagnosis of ACM, the International Task Force Criteria distinguish between minor and major ACM criteria, with an emphasis on family history, conduction defects, morphological and microstructural changes, repolarization defects, and arrhythmias. In the management and prevention of sudden cardiac death and ventricular tachyarrhythmias, epicardial and endocardial ablation with electromagnetic mapping and the use of an implantable cardiac defibrillator have emerged as useful approaches. We provide an overview of the genetics, histological features, molecular mechanisms, clinical presentation, diagnosis, biomarkers and treatment advances of ACM, including gene therapy, small-molecule and drug-based therapies, implantable cardioverter defibrillators, radiofrequency ablation, lifestyle interventions, heart transplantation and prognosis.

papers.abstract_full: Cyclopia, is an extremely rare congenital condition resulting from severe disruption of early brain and facial development and is typically lethal before or shortly after birth. We examined two infants buried together in a Middle Nasca-period cemetery in Jauranga, southern Peru. One infant, JA13A, exhibited a single median orbit and other skeletal features diagnostic of cyclopia, whereas JA13B showed no comparable congenital variations. Ancient DNA revealed an extra copy of chromosome 13 in JA13A, identifying trisomy 13 as the likely cause. The two maternally unrelated individuals were interred together in a ceramic vessel, a mortuary treatment well documented for Nasca children. By integrating skeletal, genomic, and archaeological evidence, this case provides a view of a severe congenital condition and its mortuary treatment in a past society.

papers.abstract_full: Alzheimer's disease (AD) exhibits high clinical and biological heterogeneity, which complicates the development of one-size-fits-all therapeutic strategies. Standard trial designs can mask subgroup-specific effects, highlighting the need to move towards precision neurology entailing multisystem genomics, biomarkers, and artificial intelligence (AI) integrative signals. The aim of the study is to critically synthesize and evaluate emerging strategies for drug optimization and individual therapeutic algorithms informed by genomic architecture, pharmacogenomics (PGx), and polygenic risk scores (PRS) with the opinion to resolve the controversy and unanswered question. Amplify the convergence into amyloid processing, lipid metabolism, and innate immunity seen from monogenic mutations and over 80 GWAS risk loci. Genotyping of CYP2D6 and CYP2C19 variants permits pharmacogenomic stratifications for the optimization of cholinesterase inhibitor and psychotropic dosing, thereby reducing adverse events. Variants of the alleles APOE ε4 and immune-related factors (e.g., FCGR3A) are significant in predicting the effects of ARIA associated with amyloid on anti-amyloid immunotherapy outcomes. PRS and deep phenotyping (including digital and fluid-based biomarkers) allow for the identification of unique biological endotypes (e.g., tau-dominant vs. vascular-inflammatory) that improve clinical trial enrichment and prognostication. This framework delineates molecular endotypes and translates CYP2D6 or APOE stratification into drug dosing and ARIA risk predictions. These biomarker-driven strategies shift AD management from a passive, reactive therapeutic scheme to an active, personalized one. Utilization of high-dimensional data streams via AI-driven learning health systems converts AD management from a reactive, symptom-based model to that which is proactive and hallmark biomarker-driven precision.

Current mtPRS methods primarily use three approaches: (1) aggregating genome-wide association studies (GWAS) summary statistics; (2) combining individual PRSs with weights from Principal Component Analysis (PCA); or (3) combining individual PRSs with multivariate or penalized regression-derived weights. papers.abstract_full: Multi-trait Polygenic Risk Score (mtPRS) methods improve prediction accuracy compared to single-trait PRS (stPRS) by integrating genetically correlated traits. Current mtPRS methods primarily use three approaches: (1) aggregating genome-wide association studies (GWAS) summary statistics; (2) combining individual PRSs with weights from Principal Component Analysis (PCA); or (3) combining individual PRSs with multivariate or penalized regression-derived weights. However, existing mtPRS methods face two main challenges: (1) selected variants are often non-causal, lowering prediction power; and (2) no method is universally superior across diverse genetic architectures and multi-trait correlation structures. To improve prediction performance and robustness, we propose mtPRS-FIMEL (multi-trait Polygenic Risk Score using FIne-Mapping and Ensemble Learning), an ensemble learning approach that integrates fine-mapping with multi-trait PRS construction. mtPRS-FIMEL computes mtPRS by combining multiple complementary mtPRS and stPRS methods and strategically leveraging causal variants identified through fine-mapping analysis. Specifically, it uses GWAS summary statistics to estimate causal effects and learn optimal weights for a set of PRSs from complementary mtPRS (including mtPRS-PCA, a PCA based method, and mtPRS-ML, an elastic-net based machine learning method, and stPRS). Our extensive simulations demonstrate that mtPRS-FIMEL outperforms existing mtPRS and stPRS methods in terms of prediction accuracy, PRS association strength, and patient stratification performance in the simulation settings examined. Validation with PGx GWAS data from a randomized clinical trial successfully predicted the drug response of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) change from baseline, while integrating three LDL-C-related traits (LDL, HDL, and Triglycerides) from disease GWAS, confirming its promising performance and robustness via a proof-of-concept internally cross-validated approach.

papers.abstract_full: INTRODUCTION: Polygenic risk score (PRS) is a valuable tool for predicting the risk of breast cancer (BC). However, limited studies have been conducted in Chinese women. This study aimed to develop and validate a PRS which could be used to identify individuals with high risk of breast cancer. The associations between the PRS and patients' clinicopathological characteristics or survival outcomes were also evaluated. METHODS: We developed a PRS based on genome-wide association studies (GWAS)-identified risk variants with a three-stage design across four cohorts. In total, 7,056 patients and 6,659 controls were enrolled from Fujian Medical University Union Hospital (FJMUUH) and Shanghai Breast Cancer Genetics Study (SBCGS). Five approaches were utilized to calculate the PRS, including repeated logistic regression (RLR), logistic ridge regression (LRR), artificial neural network (ANN), random forest (RF) and support vector machine (SVM). Logistic regression analyses were performed to assess the association between established PRS and clinicopathological characteristics. The correlation between PRS and patients' survival outcomes was evaluated by Cox regression models. RESULTS: Overall, 7 SNPs were selected for PRS development. PRSLRR achieved robust and stable performance across cohorts, yielding an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.633 and an OR of 1.64 per 1 SD increase. Women in the top5% and 80-95% percentiles of PRS had a 4.32-fold and a 1.40-fold elevated risk of developing breast cancer compared with those at average risk (PRS in 40-60th percentiles). The predictive performance of PRS for patients with human epidermal growth factor receptor-2 (HER-2) positive tumors was demonstrated to be higher than that of HER-2 negative tumors (AUC = 0.671 vs. 0.623). It was also identified that the PRS was not correlated with age at diagnosis or tumor characteristics. In multivariable Cox models, high PRS was associated with worse overall survival (OS) in the overall cohort (adjusted HR = 1.39, 95%CI = 1.08-1.78, p = 0.010) and unfavorable disease-free survival (DFS) (adjusted HR = 1.41, 95%CI = 1.03-1.95; p = 0.035)/OS (adjusted HR = 1.64, 95%CI = 1.14-2.37, p = 0.008) in estrogen receptor (ER) negative patients. CONCLUSION: The PRS could provide additional information for Chinese women at high risk of breast cancer and holds significant value for BC screening. An increase in PRS also indicates an unfavorable prognosis and might play a crucial role in the clinical management of breast cancer patients at the time of diagnosis.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Hypertension and type 2 diabetes (T2D) frequently coexist, but whether hypertension independently contributes to earlier diabetes onset beyond shared metabolic and genetic susceptibility remains incompletely understood. This study investigates the longitudinal relationship between hypertension and subsequent T2D risk using survival analysis and survival machine learning approaches. METHODS: A matched cohort analysis was conducted using UK Biobank participants free of diabetes at baseline, and a 6-month lag period was applied to reduce reverse causation. Time-to-event analyses were performed using Cox proportional hazards models. Genetic susceptibility was evaluated using both a genome-wide polygenic risk score (PRS) and a targeted multi-variant score (TMS). Survival machine learning models including XGBoost, Random Survival Forests, and ridge-penalized Cox regression were evalueted under identical train/test splits. Additional robustness analyses incorporated antihypertensive medication classes, genetic principal components, broader hypertension phenotype definitions integrating blood pressure measurements and medication use, stricter baseline diabetes exclusion criteria, extended lag-period analyses, and time-stratified sensitivity analyses. RESULTS: The final multivariable matched analytic cohort included 76,439 participants (37,951 individuals with HTN and 38,488 matched controls). During follow-up, 4,315 incident T2D events occurred, including 3,571 among individuals with HTN and 744 among controls. Hypertension remained independently associated with T2D after adjustment for adiposity, lipid traits, statin use, antihypertensive medication classes, genetic principal components, and genetic susceptibility (HR 1.30, p < 0.001). Individuals with hypertension developed T2D earlier, with reduced diabetes-free survival over follow-up. Both PRS and TMS independently predicted T2D risk and demonstrated significant interactions with hypertension. Survival machine learning analyses showed progressive improvement in discrimination following incorporation of hypertension and genetic susceptibility, with XGBoost demonstrating the highest performance (C-index 0.823, 95% CI 0.812-0.833). Importantly, the observed association remained robust across multiple sensitivity analyses, demonstrating persistence of the association beyond the early post-index period. CONCLUSIONS: Hypertension is associated with an increased and earlier T2D risk independent of metabolic risk factors and genetic susceptibility. Polygenic risk further stratifies diabetes risk but does not explain the relationship between hypertension and earlier T2D onset. The consistency of the findings across sensitivity analyses and survival-learning frameworks supports hypertension as an important component of the cardiometabolic trajectory preceding T2D development.

papers.abstract_full: Background  Genomic studies in hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) are limited by sample sizes and targeted approaches. Methods  The Genomic Studies in Blood and Marrow Transplantation (GS-BMT) project is a collaboration between the National Cancer Institute (NCI) and the CIBMTR® designed to investigate recipient and donor determinants of HCT outcomes. We are generating genome-wide SNP-array genotyping for all samples, and sequencing and methylation profiling for selected subsets. We report study design and cohort characteristics and present two proof-of-concept analyses: comparison of conventional and machine learning prediction of overall survival after HCT in 9,262 patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML), and assessment of inherited susceptibility to clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) among 19,750 HCT donors using polygenic scores (PGS). Results  GS-BMT includes 30,718 donor–recipient pairs who received allogeneic HCT in the United States between 2000 and 2019. In AML, clinical variables alone provided modest prediction for post-transplant survival, with similar performance for Cox proportional hazards, random survival forest, and deep neural network survival models (C-index=0.63, 0.62, and 0.62, respectively). In donors, CHIP-PGS did not differ by age (p=0.76) but was modestly lower in unrelated  vs . related donors (−0.06 standard deviation [SD]; p=0.002). In an illustrative analysis assuming risk of event increases by 50% or 80% per PGS-SD, the top 5.2% and 12.3% of the donors, respectively, would have at least twice the risk of a donor with the average PGS.  Conclusions  GS-BMT establishes a large genomic platform aiming to improve individualized risk prediction, donor selection, and precision medicine in HCT.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Three-dimensional fast spin-echo MR cisternography (CUBE) of the internal auditory canal (IAC) and cerebellopontine angle (CPA) requires longer acquisition times that can limit clinical throughput. We evaluated whether a deep learning (DL)-based highly accelerated reconstruction technique, Sonic DL`™ (SDL), combined with a commercially available DL denoising reconstruction (AIR™ Recon DL, ARDL), preserves or improves subjective image quality and cochlear anatomy visualization relative to standard CUBE-ARDL while shortening scan time. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Consecutive patients underwent brain MRI for suspected IAC pathology at 1.5T and 3T with paired acquisition of standard 3D CUBE-ARDL and an accelerated 3D CUBE-SDL sequence. Both used the same voxel size at 1.5T (0.6x0.6x1.2 mm3) and 3T (0.6x0.6x0.6 mm3). Scan times for CUBE-ARDL versus CUBE-SDL were 2:33 versus 1:41 min at 1.5T and 1:55 versus 1:11 min at 3T. Two independent neuroradiologists blinded to MRI acquisition method scored randomized, de-identified images on a 5-point Likert scale across five domains (overall image quality, noise, sharpness, artifacts, cochlear anatomy visualization). Reader-averaged scores for CUBE-ARDL and CUBE-SDL were compared with paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, with reader-specific and cumulative link mixed model (CLMM) sensitivity analyses and false discovery rate (FDR) adjustment; intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) quantified inter-reader reliability for each technique; Gwet's AC2 and weighted (Conger's) kappa with linear ordinal weights quantified pooled inter-reader agreement. RESULTS: After exclusion of 5 training cases per field strength, 49 (1.5T) and 34 (3T) patients were analyzed. CUBE-SDL scored significantly better than CUBE-ARDL for all five domains at both field strengths (all FDR-adjusted P < .001), consistently for each reader and in the CLMM. Inter-reader reliability (ICC) for CUBE-SDL was moderate-to-excellent at 3T (0.63-0.92) and moderate at 1.5T (0.65-0.74), generally exceeding CUBE-ARDL (3T: 0.35-0.61; 1.5T: 0.50-0.71). Pooled inter-reader agreement (Gwet's AC2) ranged from 0.56 to 0.89. CONCLUSIONS: A combined Sonic DL acceleration with ARDL-denoised reconstruction for 3D T2 CUBE produced significantly higher subjective image quality at both 1.5T and 3T, and, at 3T, higher inter-reader reliability than standard CUBE-ARDL, while shortening acquisition time by 34%-38%. These findings support further evaluation, including diagnostic accuracy studies, of CUBE-SDL as an alternative to CUBE-ARDL.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT  The mammillary bodies are a central component of the hippocampal–diencephalic-cingulate network that is critically involved in emotion processing and memory function, yet their genetic architecture remains unknown. papers.abstract_full: ABSTRACT  The mammillary bodies are a central component of the hippocampal–diencephalic-cingulate network that is critically involved in emotion processing and memory function, yet their genetic architecture remains unknown. We conducted a genome-wide association study (GWAS) of mammillary body volume in 38,064 participants from the UK Biobank and replicated our findings in the Rhineland Study cohort (N = 4,860). Mammillary body and hypothalamic subregional volumes were derived from structural brain MRIs using FastSurfer-HypVINN, an established and validated deep learning-based segmentation tool. Univariate GWAS identified 34 genomic loci associated with mammillary body volume, including 26 novel loci, with 20 loci showing replication in the Rhineland Study. Meta-analysis across both cohorts (N = 42,924) identified 44 associated loci, of which 35 were novel. Multivariate GWAS of hypothalamic subregions identified 55 loci, including 40 novel associations. Integrative cross-omics analyses identified  MEI1 and CAPZA1 as key molecular candidates, with genetically regulated  MEI1 expression and circulating CAPZA1 protein levels partially mediating genetic effects on mammillary body volume. Genetic correlation and Mendelian randomization analyses further revealed a bidirectional relationship between mammillary body volume and major depressive disorder. Together, our findings elucidate the genetic architecture of mammillary body volume and its relation to mental disorders.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: MYBPC3 truncating variants (MYBPC3tv) represent the most common genetic substrate in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, yet carriers show substantial phenotypic variability despite a shared mechanism of haploinsufficiency. The contribution of additional genetic variants to this variability remains incompletely defined. METHODS: We analyzed 11 991 unrelated hypertrophic cardiomyopathy probands undergoing clinical genetic testing. Analyses focused on MYBPC3tv carriers stratified by additional intermediate-effect variants (IEVs) or second monogenic variants. IEVs were further classified as sarcomeric or nonsarcomeric. All probands were genetically characterized at a single center using standardized sequencing protocols, with uniform ascertainment of IEVs throughout the study period. Primary outcomes included age-related penetrance, maximal left ventricular wall thickness, and major adverse cardiovascular events; independent predictors were assessed by a multivariable Cox regression model. RESULTS: Among 2767 genotype-positive probands, MYBPC3 accounted for 47.6% of cases, with truncating variants representing 81.9% of MYBPC3-positive individuals. Within MYBPC3tv carriers, additional variants were associated with a stepwise gradient of disease severity. Median age at diagnosis decreased from 48 years in isolated carriers to 42 years in MYBPC3tv+IEV and 28 years in double-monogenic carriers, whereas mean wall thickness increased from 21.3 to 24.1 and 26.3 mm, respectively. In multivariable analyses, cumulative genetic burden remained an independent predictor of major adverse cardiovascular event. Sarcomeric IEV carriers (hazard ratio, 10.3 [95% CI, 2.3-28.7]) and biallelic MYBPC3 carriers (hazard ratio, 23.2 [95% CI, 5.3-115.0]) exhibited the highest risk, although estimates in these subgroups should be interpreted cautiously given the limited number of events. All biallelic MYBPC3 carriers were diagnosed in childhood. CONCLUSIONS: Cumulative rare variant burden explains a subset of the phenotypic heterogeneity among MYBPC3tv carriers, defining a hierarchical gradient of disease expression. Intermediate-effect alleles and second monogenic variants, particularly biallelic MYBPC3, identify higher-risk subgroups that may benefit from intensified surveillance, individualized management, and guided therapies.

CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory cohort, WES did not detect a clear rare coding variant burden signal associated with apical aneurysm.

papers.abstract_full: Although cognitive decline and dementia are common at advanced ages, a fraction of individuals reach extreme ages maintaining high levels of cognitive function. Here, we compared whole-exome sequencing data from 136 cognitive superagers, individuals whose memory performance matches normative expectations for persons ~30 years younger, to 114 average-cognition controls and the gnomAD population reference database. While standard single-variant and burden analyses did not identify exome-wide significant loci, a rare variant allele frequency analysis identified 114 significant rare coding variants enriched in cognitive superagers. We highlight ten significant missense variants in genes implicating neurovascular biology (LOX, CLEC4M, CBWD6), immune regulation (HLA-B, HLA-DRB1, ITGAX, MUC4, MUC1), and neuronal structural (CEP131 x2). Together, these findings support an extreme-phenotype strategy as a tractable discovery framework for rare coding variation and nominate a set of biologically plausible loci to reveal potential genetic mechanisms for resilience to age-related cognitive impairment.

papers.abstract_full: Short QT Syndrome (SQTS) is a rare cardiac channelopathy characterized by abnormally short QTc intervals and increased sudden cardiac death (SCD) risk. Only 20-30% of SQTS cases have been linked to genetic mutations, typically in surface membrane ion channels. We identified a novel lysosomal  TMEM175 gene mutation (p.Arg377His) in 7 patients in a family with SQTS and SCD. Genetic analyses, including whole exome sequencing in the family and rare-variant burden testing in ∼118,000 UK Biobank participants, suggested an association between  TMEM175 rare variants and QT interval shortening. Functional studies in CRISPR-engineered mice and patient-specific induced pluripotent stem cellderived cardiomyocytes (iPSC-CMs) revealed that TMEM175  R377H causes shortened QT intervals and hastened repolarization, respectively, as well an increased arrhythmia susceptibility. Isolated TMEM175  R377H cardiomyocytes showed action potential duration (APD) abbreviation, confirmed in whole TMEM175  R377H mouse hearts and patient-specific iPSC-CM monolayers. In silico and electron microscopy studies showed that TMEM175  R377H disrupts lysosomal-mitochondrial interactions, leading to mitochondrial dysfunction, as evidenced by the reduced maximal respiration and spare respiratory capacity, with reduced ATP production, I  KATP activation, and APD shortening. This mutation represents the first non-sarcolemmal ion channel defect associated with SQTS and high SCD risk, potentially expanding the genetic landscape of the disease.

Breast cancer genome-w…
papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: The plasma proteome may help connect inherited breast cancer susceptibility to biologically interpretable and potentially actionable pathways, but proteome-wide evidence across ancestries remains limited. METHODS: We conducted proteome-wide Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses of breast cancer risk using cis-protein quantitative trait loci for 1,962 distinct plasma proteins from 34,557 European-ancestry participants in the UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project. Breast cancer genome-wide association studies included 156,901 cases and 204,634 controls of European, East Asian, and African ancestries. Ancestry-specific MR estimates were combined by fixed-effects meta-analysis. Candidate proteins were further evaluated through subtype-specific and reverse-direction MR analyses, statistical colocalization, replication in independent European and East Asian proteomic datasets, and analyses of associations between protein polygenic scores and breast cancer status in All of Us. RESULTS: Twelve proteins achieved Bonferroni significance in the cross-ancestry meta-analysis (P < 0.05/1,971 tests), including eight previously reported proteins and four newly prioritized by MR. DNPH1 showed cross-ancestry heterogeneity, while CASP8, RALB, and USP28 showed cross-subtype heterogeneity after accounting for shared controls (all P < 0.05/12). Complementary support varied: six candidates showed strong colocalization (PPH4 ≥ 0.80); four replicated with a consistent direction and nominal significance in deCODE, two in the Japan COVID-19 Task Force, and four in All of Us (all P < 0.05). The strongest cumulative support was observed for LRRC25, PARK7, and LRRC37A2. CONCLUSIONS: These findings prioritize circulating protein candidates for mechanistic, prevention-oriented, and translational follow-up in breast cancer, while underscoring the need for larger ancestrally diverse proteomic resources to support equitable target and biomarker discovery.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Substance use disorders (SUDs) are moderately to highly heritable and develop in stages that typically begin in adolescence or young adulthood. The predominant use of cross-sectional adult samples to study SUDs and their genetic liability leaves it unclear whether their correlates may plausibly reflect predispositional risk and/or arise as a consequence of exposure. METHODS: We conducted a phenome-wide association study (PheWAS) of polygenic scores (PGSs) for SUDs (i.e., problematic alcohol use, tobacco use disorder, cannabis use disorder [CUD], opioid use disorder [OUD], and a general addiction risk factor) in children ages 8 to 13 years (n European ancestry = 5556; n African American ancestry = 1584) enrolled in the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study. Up to 1697 phenotypes were examined across several domains, including mental health, substance use, physical health, cognition, and screen media. RESULTS: The PheWAS yielded 309 significant associations with the SUD PGS, particularly among mental health, sleep, screen time, and caffeine consumption phenotypes. Most associations remained significant in substance-naïve participants. The CUD PGS had the largest number of associations and was particularly associated with externalizing behavior in both genetic ancestry subsamples. OUD PGS associations were enriched for cognitive and neighborhood environmental phenotypes. Neuroimaging phenotypes (e.g., resting-state functional connectivity) partially accounted for associations between the SUD PGS and screen time phenotypes. CONCLUSIONS: Genetic liability to SUDs is expressed during childhood as potentially modifiable risk factors that could be targeted to attenuate its expression in adolescence and adulthood. Genetic liability to substance use disorders is expressed in youth before substance use onset. Among up to 5556 children ages 8 to 13 years, a higher genetic predisposition to substance use disorders was linked to mental health symptoms, sleep issues, and higher screen time and media use. Identifying these early, potentially modifiable indicators offers clear targets for future research and the development of early interventions.

papers.abstract_full: Background: Low-count monoclonal B-cell lymphocytosis (LC-MBL) is a precursor to chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL). Forty-one inherited susceptibility variants for CLL have been reported, but whether these variants impact CLL, through the initiation of the clone (LC-MBL) or progression of LC-MBL to CLL, is not well characterized. Methods: We evaluated 41 previously reported CLL susceptibility variants and the CLL polygenic risk score (CLL-PRS, a weighted score of the 41 variants) among a study of 8322 individuals who screened negative for MBL based on eight-color flow cytometry, 1601 individuals who screened positive for LC-MBL, and 2606 CLL patients. Logistic regression was used to estimate odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) for LC-MBL compared with MBL-negative individuals and for CLL compared with LC-MBL (herein labeled progression). Models were adjusted for age, sex, and genetic principal components. Results: Of the 41 variants, 22 (54%) were associated with LC-MBL and 20 (49%) with progression (all p < 0.05). The ORs for eight variants differed between LC-MBL risk and progression (false discovery rate, FDR < 0.05), including two (rs6708784, 2q13; rs391855, 16q24.1) with associations in opposite directions. The CLL-PRS was associated with both LC-MBL (OR = 1.77, 95% CI: 1.66-1.88, p = 3.7 × 10-68) and progression (OR = 1.45, 95% CI: 1.35-1.56, p = 8.1 × 10-24). Conclusions: The effects of individual CLL-risk variants vary across the etiological continuum of disease with a subset associated with clonal initiation of LC-MBL and clonal progression to different degrees, or even in opposite directions. The CLL-PRS may help identify individuals at elevated risk for both LC-MBL and progression to CLL.

papers.abstract_full: PURPOSE: Open-angle glaucoma (OAG) is the leading cause of irreversible blindness and is highly heritable. Despite effective treatments, approximately 50% of cases remain undiagnosed. We aimed to develop and validate a clinically applicable, genetics-based risk prediction tool for OAG across diverse ancestries. DESIGN: Genetic association study and risk prediction analysis. PARTICIPANTS: More than 6 million individuals contributing genome-wide association study data from multiple ancestry groups. METHODS: We constructed a comprehensive polygenic risk score (PRS) for OAG using a multitrait modeling framework that integrated glaucoma-related traits, including intraocular pressure, optic disc parameters, and ocular hypertension. PRS performance was evaluated for OAG risk across major ancestry groups and assessed for associations with age at diagnosis, treatment escalation, surgical outcomes, and familial risk. papers.abstract_full: To develop a labeled image dataset of suspected carotid artery calcifications (CACs) on dental panoramic radiographs (PRs) and to propose a deep learning-based framework for their automated detection and segmentation. A retrospective dataset comprising 19,205 PRs obtained from our institution (between 2015 and 2023) was analyzed. After manual labeling, 372 images showing CACs and 322 controls were included. A hybrid architecture combining FasTVit, AttentionNet, and DC-UNet was implemented for classification, detection, and segmentation. Model performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, the Dice coefficient, intersection over union (IoU), and area under the curve (AUC). The study evaluated two scenarios: one in which detection and segmentation were performed after classification, and another in which the classification was omitted. The classification model achieved an accuracy of 0.8780, a precision of 0.8779, a recall of 0.8795, and a specificity of, 0.8795. Incorporating the classification step improved precision from 0.48 to 0.93, accuracy from 0.79 to 0.97, and specificity from 0.75 to 0.98. The final framework achieved an area under the ROC curve of 0.96. The proposed hybrid artificial intelligence (AI) framework showed promising internal performance for the opportunistic detection and localization of radiographic findings suggestive of CACs on PRs. Within the limitations of this study, the proposed framework may serve as a complementary aid to dentists by flagging suspected CACs during routine interpretation of PRs and facilitating timely referral for confirmatory cardiovascular assessment.

papers.abstract_full: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a behaviorally defined, biologically heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition with high heritability, estimated at 0.83 (95% CI 0.79-0.87) in Swedish population data. Large-scale exome sequencing, copy-number variant analysis, and genome-wide association studies have implicated a growing number of genes and genomic loci in autism liability, and functional genomic work has repeatedly converged on mid-gestational cortical development. In parallel, prenatal genetics has moved from karyotyping to chromosomal microarray analysis, exome and genome sequencing, and screening based on cell-free DNA in maternal plasma. This review asks how far these developments allow genetic susceptibility to autism to be identified before birth, and what prevents such identification from constituting prediction or diagnosis of autism in an individual fetus. It organizes the evidence in four steps - analytic validity (can the variant be detected in fetal DNA)?, variant interpretation (can it be classified under ACMG/AMP and ACMG-ClinGen standards)?, clinical validity (how far does it shift the probability of autism)?, and clinical utility (does knowing it improve outcomes)? - which makes explicit the classification step within the conventional three-stage sequence and locates where translation breaks down. A second distinction, between molecular diagnosis of a genetic condition and diagnosis of autism itself, runs alongside it. Recurrent copy-number variants such as 16p11.2 and 15q11-q13 rearrangements, and pathogenic variants in genes such as CHD8, SCN2A, SHANK3, and PTEN, are technically detectable by currently available prenatal diagnostic genomic platforms when such testing is clinically indicated. Their interpretation is frequently incomplete, their clinical validity for autism specifically is limited by incomplete penetrance, variable expressivity, and pleiotropy, and their clinical utility for neurodevelopmental prediction is unestablished. Common polygenic variation contributes substantially to population-level liability, but individual-level discrimination is poor and ancestry portability is limited. Prenatal diagnostic genomic testing is additionally largely indication-driven rather than a population screen for neurodevelopmental risk. Prenatal sequencing may therefore establish a molecular diagnosis of a condition associated with an increased likelihood of autism; this is not prenatal diagnosis of autism. Progress will require ancestrally diverse cohorts, population-based penetrance estimates, longitudinal prenatal-to-childhood follow-up, and probabilistic multimodal models, alongside counseling standards that resist deterministic interpretation.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: We investigated genetic variations driving young age-at-diabetes-diagnosis (ADD) and developed a genetic risk score (GRS) to identify Chinese individuals at risk of young-onset diabetes (YOD with ADD<40). METHODS: We performed genome-wide association studies (GWAS) for ADD with internal and external replication in 22,611 individuals with type 2 diabetes (T2D, 20% with YOD) and identified Chinese-prioritized loci by conditioning on the polygenic risk score (PRS) of ADD constructed from publicly available datasets. We constructed ADD-GRS using genome-wide independent variants (p<5E-08) and examined its associations with glycemic traits in diabetes and non-diabetes cohorts. RESULTS: We identified three independent signals at genome-wide significance (P < 5×10-8) mapping to CDKAL1 (rs2206734, β=-0.75 (SE:0.13) per copy of T allele, effect allele frequency (EAF)=0.38, p=2.12E-09), PAX4 (rs61160304, β=-1.01 (SE:0.17) per copy of T allele, EAF=0.19, p=2.51E-09), and KCNQ1 (rs2299620, β=-0.77 (SE:0.14) per copy of G allele, EAF=0.70, p=2.80E-08). The variants at PAX4 and KCNQ1 were independent of the genetic liability estimated by ADD-PRS from Europeans and South Indians. In the diabetes cohort, the ADD-GRS was associated with younger ADD, lower C-peptide, higher HbA1c and pathway-specific T2D-PRS for beta-cell+proinsulin and residual glycemia. Using YOD versus later-onset diabetes as a secondary outcome, LINC02783/PADI1 (rs72895704, OR:1.52 per copy of A allele, EAF=0.02, p=1.93E-06) and TARS2P1 (rs145218437, OR: 1.73 per copy of C allele, EAF=0.02, p=7.57E-08) showed suggestive significance. CONCLUSIONS: Both known and novel T2D loci contribute to ADD in Chinese people and may be used to detect high risk individuals for early intervention to prevent or delay onset of YOD.

papers.abstract_full: Accumulating evidence has suggested that depression is associated with an increased risk of Parkinson's disease (PD), yet whether pre-clinical depressive symptoms in PD development and the potential mediating effects of metabolomic profiles remain unclear. We aimed to examine the association between depressive symptoms and PD risk, evaluate effect modification by genetic susceptibility, and assess metabolomic mediation. This prospective study included 451,922 PD-free participants from the UK Biobank. Depressive symptoms were collected by a 2-item Patient Health Questionnaire (range, 0-6; ≥3 indicates possible depressive disorder) at baseline. Identification of PD was based on medical records. PD-related polygenic risk score (PRSPD), which incorporates established genes for PD based on external GWAS meta-analyses, was tertiled as low, moderate, and high. Baseline plasma metabolites were quantified via NMR spectroscopy from blood samples. Data were analyzed using Cox regression. Over a median follow-up of 14.6 years, 3108 (0.7%) participants developed PD. Higher depressive symptom severity showed linear association with PD risk (hazard ratio [HR]: 1.11, 95% confidence interval: 1.07-1.15). Participants with possible depressive disorder had 36% higher PD risk (HR: 1.36, 1.15-1.61). Those with both possible depressive disorder and high genetic risk had the highest PD risk (HR 2.15, 1.74-2.65; P for interaction = 0.028). Metabolomic signature, incorporating fatty acids and lipoproteins, accounted for 15% (model-based proportion) of the depressive symptoms-PD association. Pre-clinical depressive symptoms are associated with a moderately increased risk of PD, particularly among people with a high genetic susceptibility to PD. Metabolomic profiles account for a significant portion of this relationship.

papers.abstract_full: Most genome-wide association studies (GWASs) and polygenic score (PGS) models for lung function are based on European-ancestry individuals. Here, we performed GWASs in 17,738 Chinese individuals from the Dongfeng-Tongji (DFTJ) and Wuhan-Zhuhai (WHZH) cohorts, followed by meta-analysis with lung function GWASs from the China Kadoorie Biobank (sample size, n = 100,285), the Taiwan Biobank (n = 62,901), and European-ancestry studies (n = 400,102). Multi-ancestry fine-mapping pinpoints four novel candidate causal variants: one insertion (rs56381615, LINC02270) and three SNPs (rs6941411, PTK7; rs13315867, EPHA3; and rs2713769, ABI3BP). Cross-ancestry genetic correlations are high (0.682-0.811) but significantly lower than 1 (p < 0.005). Transcriptome-wide association analysis across 16 tissues identifies 1,374 genes, including PTK7, CUL7, and EPHA3 as leading novel candidates. Finally, we develop multi-ancestry PGS models that outperform existing models. Overall, this study quantifies cross-ancestry genetic correlation, prioritizes candidate genes, and enhances PGS prediction accuracy of lung function traits in East Asian populations.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Breastfeeding has established health benefits for infants and has been associated with postpartum improved maternal cardiometabolic health in the long term. However, breastfeeding prevalence is also inversely associated with prepartum body mass index (BMI), and both are linked to socioeconomic factors. We sought to clarify the relationship between prepartum BMI and breastfeeding prevalence in the Million Veteran Program (MVP), a large-scale genetic epidemiology study of US Veterans. METHODS: We included data from parous female participants with available breastfeeding information from the MVP cohort. BMI at enrollment as well as earliest BMI available were extracted from the electronic health record, and polygenic scores (PGS) for BMI were calculated for the subset of participants with genotype data. We modeled whether participants breastfed an infant for one month or more (BF ≥ 1 M) as a function of BMI at enrollment (n = 20,293); earliest BMI where available pre-pregnancy (n = 532); and PGS for BMI among genetically inferred European ancestry participants (n = 11,568). We conducted Mendelian randomization for breastfeeding using PGS as an instrumental variable. RESULTS: A higher BMI predicted a lower likelihood of BF ≥ 1 M in all analyses. A + 5 kg/m2 BMI pre-pregnancy was associated with a 24% reduced odds of BF ≥ 1 M, and a + 5 kg/m2 genetically predicted BMI was associated with a 17% reduced odds of BF ≥ 1 M. CONCLUSIONS: BMI predicts a lower likelihood of BF ≥ 1 M. Given the high success of breastfeeding initiation in supportive environments combined with potential health benefits to both infant and mother, pregnant Veterans with prepartum elevated BMI may benefit from additional postpartum breastfeeding support.

papers.abstract_full: IntroductionIntegrating genomic testing within primary care settings like Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs) is uncommon despite its potential to improve health outcomes. Understanding patient experiences receiving genomic testing in a FQHC highlights the systemic, equity, and community influences that genomic testing can have in diverse primary care settings.MethodsThis study was a qualitative cross-sectional case study of 11 Latino patients within a FQHC in Phoenix, AZ who received polygenic risk scores (PRS) and/or monogenic testing as part of the eMERGE network research studies. Qualitative thematic data analysis was conducted using NVivo software according to a codebook. Themes and findings were co-derived by the study team and the FQHC's community engagement board (CAB) to ensure representative data analysis.ResultsThree central themes emerged through analyzing patient interviews: the FQHC context, impact on the family system, and socioeconomic consequences of genomic testing implementation.ConclusionParticipants expressed an overall openness to receiving genomic testing as FQHC patients, referring to how their genomic test results impacted their family health decision-making. This study revealed downstream impacts of genomic testing implementation in a FQHC setting, specifically socioeconomic challenges related to access, concerns surrounding follow-up, specialist referral, and continuity of care.
