papers.abstract_full: Liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) drives the formation of membraneless organelles (MLOs) that regulate cellular compartmentalization and diverse biological processes. However, the landscape and clinical relevance of MLO-associated activity in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remain unclear. We integrated curated MLO-associated gene sets with transcriptomic data to estimate MLO activity using single-sample gene set enrichment analysis. MLO-related molecular subtypes were identified via consensus clustering, and an integrative machine learning framework was used to develop and validate the Membraneless Organelle Risk Score (MLORS) across independent cohorts. We further examined associations of MLORS with immune features, genomic alterations, and predicted treatment sensitivity and evaluated the function and phase-separation properties of E2F7 in vitro. MLO-associated activity was broadly dysregulated in LUAD, with high-MLO and low-MLO subtypes exhibiting distinct immune profiles and survival outcomes. High MLORS was associated with poorer survival, a computationally inferred immune-suppressed microenvironmental profile, higher tumor mutational burden, and lower predicted sensitivity to selected EGFR-targeted agents and chemotherapy. E2F7 formed nuclear condensates with LLPS-like properties and promoted lung cancer cell proliferation and migration in vitro. These findings link transcriptionally inferred MLO activity to the heterogeneity and prognosis of LUAD, support MLORS as a candidate prognostic stratification tool, and identify E2F7 phase-separation behavior as a potential therapeutic vulnerability.

papers.abstract_full: Translating candidate gene panels into objective physiological trait interpretations remains a major hurdle in exercise genomics. Conventional total genotype scoring suffers from severe panel-composition bias, fails to evaluate unannotated or novel variants, and frequently fosters inflated claims regarding individual athletic prediction. Here, we present a population-calibrated, multi-tiered computational framework that evaluates genomic variation across six evidence streams integrating deep learning protein and genomic language models (ESM-2, Evo 2), missense and splice predictors (AlphaMissense, SpliceAI), and regional pathogenic-density metrics to generate a continuous Variant Priority Score (VPS; 1-10 scale). By dynamically renormalizing missing evidence streams rather than zero-filling them, the framework robustly scores unannotated variants lacking empirical database entries. Individual trait burden across 344 genes (spanning 17 physiological traits in Aerobic, Anaerobic, and Recovery domains) is aggregated and normalized against ancestry-matched expectations derived from gnomAD South Asian and an in-house reference cohort (N > 13,000). When applied to 960 South Indian individuals (584 male, 376 female; whole-exome sequencing), this normalization removed the dependence of expected trait burden on panel size by construction, and gene count explained only 2.7% of the variance in the resulting capacity scores (six traits interrogated by 16 to 33 genes). Variance partitioning of 4,764 individual-by-trait scores (six of the 17 traits: one aerobic, two anaerobic and three recovery) revealed that score variation was predominantly trait-driven (45.5%) rather than individual-driven (11.1%, p = 0.386), a pattern reproduced independently in males and females and with no statistically significant gender difference in capacity scores, indicating that, in this cohort, the candidate panel resolved differences between physiological traits but did not detect differences between individuals in capacity scores (no athletic phenotype was measured). Benchmarking against ClinVar classifications achieved an AUC of 0.74, which fell to 0.62 when archive-dependent streams were excluded, directly quantifying the role of shared data provenance. Replacing the in-house frequency reference with gnomAD South Asian shifted absolute scores (median fold change 0.73) but preserved trait ordering (Spearman 0.96), so scores are positions against a stated, population-specific reference. This framework provides an auditable, evidence-traceable baseline for trait-level research and functional variant prioritization while offering a critical methodological safeguard against over-interpreting unvalidated individual performance predictions.

papers.abstract_full: The development of foundation models that learn a general grammar of DNA (DNA language models) has accelerated in recent years. The vast majority of DNA large language models (LLMs), such as DNABERT-2 and Nucleotide Transformer, are pretrained almost exclusively on reference genomes. They therefore cannot represent the two sources of variation most directly tied to regulatory differences between people: genetic variants and DNA methylation. Long-read sequencing (Nanopore and PacBio) now measures both from the same native DNA molecules, but no model is designed to use this joint readout. With this in mind, we developed ModBERT, a DNA language model built on a five-letter probabilistic genome representation in which each position is a distribution over A, C, G, T, 5mC (represented with M). In pretraining, these distributions encode population allele frequencies and CpG methylation levels from 242 individuals in the 1000 Genomes Long-Read Sequencing Consortium, learned with a soft-target masked language modeling objective. We further propose probabilistic fine-tuning, in which the same representation encodes one individual's genotype and methylation. A fine-tuned model can then make person-specific predictions from a single assay. Under this novel fine-tuning framework, we show that ModBERT effectively utilizes methylation information to classify peaks from functional genomic assays, including histone mark (n=11 different marks) and transcription factor binding (n=69 TFs) ChIP-seq data, outperforming ab initio trained models and ModBERT pretrained on sequences without methylation. In silico methylation perturbations yield TF sensitivities that correlate with independent methylation-aware motif models. Using an evaluation design that separates generalization to new loci from generalization to new individuals, ModBERT predicts chromatin accessibility at held-out loci in held-out individuals (AUROC 0.88). Its predicted variant effects agree with likely causal caQTLs (Spearman correlation = 0.52) but not with variants associated only through linkage, a traditionally challenging task. Overall, ModBERT establishes a framework for personal-genome language modeling, in which a model reads each individual's genetic and epigenetic sequence rather than a shared reference. This enables in silico dissection of variant and methylation effects on gene regulation and principled prioritization of candidates for experimental validation as population-scale long-read cohorts (e.g., 1KGP and Human Pangenome Reference Consortium) grow.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Background  Endometrial cancer (EC) is strongly associated with metabolic disorders, while glycolytic reprogramming contributes to tumor progression and adverse outcomes. This study aimed to identify glycolysis-related prognostic genes and develop a machine learning-based signature for EC risk stratification. Methods  Transcriptomic and clinical data were obtained from The Cancer Genome Atlas. Glycolysis-related genes were collected from KEGG, MSigDB, and Reactome. Differential expression and univariate Cox analyses were used to identify prognostic candidates. Multiple machine learning algorithms and combinations were evaluated to construct a prognostic model. Functional enrichment, immune infiltration, somatic mutation, tumor mutational burden, and drug sensitivity analyses were performed. Single-cell RNA sequencing datasets GSE179640 and GSE173682 were analyzed to characterize CENPA expression across cell types and its clinical relevance. Results  Among 5,990 differentially expressed genes, 99 overlapped with 290 glycolysis-related genes, and 16 were associated with overall survival. Among 117 model combinations, random survival forest plus generalized boosted model generated a seven-gene signature comprising CLDN9, CENPA, GPI, TFF3, FBP1, SPAG4, and AURKA. The 1-, 3-, and 5-year AUCs were 0.88, 0.81, and 0.84 in the training cohort and 0.73, 0.77, and 0.76 in the internal validation cohort, respectively. High-risk patients had poorer survival and distinct pathway, immune, and genomic features. Single-cell analysis showed heterogeneous CENPA expression, while elevated CENPA was associated with advanced stage and poorer survival. Conclusions  The glycolysis-related signature stratified EC patients by survival risk and was associated with distinct biological features. CENPA emerged as a candidate prognostic biomarker requiring independent external validation and experimental investigation.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Background  Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) represents the most prevalent form of leukemia in adults, arising from the accumulation of multiple genetic mutations and dysregulated gene expression. The substantial molecular heterogeneity characteristic of AML contributes to variability in treatment responses, underscoring the critical importance of understanding the prognostic implications of genetic alterations for guiding therapeutic decisions. Therefore, this study aimed to identify novel genes with prognostic potential in AML patients. Methods  Transcriptomic data from adult AML patients were obtained from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) database. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) highlighted the turquoise module as the most strongly associated with survival (cor = 0.27, p = 0.002). A total of 851 hub genes from this module were retained for downstream machine learning-based feature selection using Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO), Random Survival Forest (RSF), Elastic Net (ENET), and Adaptive Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (AdaLASSO). Based on the mean selection frequency across all four algorithms, the top nine genes, LRCH4, ACOT7, TXN2, GCDH, GIGYF1, INPP5E, MVD, FIBP, and PDLIM7, were retained as the final candidate gene panel. Expression patterns of these genes were validated in an independent AML cohort (GSE37642, GPL96). Results  Among them, ACOT7, TXN2, and PDLIM7 showed significant differential expression with concordant direction across cohorts, all exhibiting upregulation (positive log₂FC) in the validation dataset. RT-qPCR validation confirmed significant upregulation of PDLIM7 (p = 0.016) and an increased expression trend of TXN2 (p = 0.710) in AML samples, consistent with bioinformatics predictions, while ACOT7 exhibited significant downregulation (p = 0.038), contrasting with the upregulation observed in the discovery dataset. Conclusions  In conclusion, based on significant differences in gene expression and bioinformatics analyses, our study identified three potential prognostic candidate genes that warrant further investigation in prognostic studies.

papers.abstract: Current cancer screening efforts face the dual problems of low patient adherence and a lack of available tests for many cancers, which motivates the development of less invasive multi-cancer early detection strategies. papers.abstract_full: Current cancer screening efforts face the dual problems of low patient adherence and a lack of available tests for many cancers, which motivates the development of less invasive multi-cancer early detection strategies. Such strategies will likely involve the use of liquid biopsies, which can analyze biomarkers found in blood for the presence of cancer. We introduce Blackjack, a new detection approach that focuses on the fragmentation patterns of plasma-derived cell-free DNA (cfDNA). Blackjack characterizes a person’s cfDNA fragmentation sites with a position probability matrix (PPM) that encodes information about the sequence context of the sites. For classification, Blackjack computes two features that represent the similarity of an individual’s PPM to those of known healthy and cancer cohorts. With these two features, Blackjack then uses logistic regression to classify a new sample as being from a healthy individual or a person with cancer. In cross-validation experiments using two external whole genome sequencing datasets, Blackjack showed high performance, achieving a minimum area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.993 and minimum sensitivity (Sn) of 91.8% (at 98% specificity). This high performance was also present for stage I (AUC 0.991, Sn 89.8%) and stage II cancers (AUC 0.993, Sn 90.2%), and across eight different cancers (minimum AUC 0.985, minimum Sn 80.0%). We demonstrate that Blackjack’s accuracy is stable at low simulated sequencing depths (∼0.24x), and that tissue of origin prediction using Blackjack’s similarity measures is high (minimum 82% accuracy of the top two predicted tissues). Our findings show that cfDNA fragmentation site contexts have valuable signals for early cancer detection, and that developing diagnostics with machine learning can benefit from a focus on having a small number of informative features.

papers.abstract: Literature reviews are among the most read and cited scholarly publications, yet most draw on one or two databases, privilege the most-cited voices and report conclusions without testing whether they depend on the choice of sources. papers.abstract_full: Literature reviews are among the most read and cited scholarly publications, yet most draw on one or two databases, privilege the most-cited voices and report conclusions without testing whether they depend on the choice of sources. Reporting guidelines secure transparency of searching and selection but do not prescribe how to balance academic, practice, policy and emerging evidence, or how to measure the robustness of conclusions. We present 360° MDL, the Multidimensional Literature Review Model, developed with a design-science approach and released with an open toolkit and a 30-item reporting checklist. It combines five evidence stream families, a three-gate selection process with a six-criterion quality gate and portfolio rules, eight analysis matrices, and indices of stream balance, coverage, method diversity and resilience; each key finding is graded by its Triangulation Strength across stream families and stress-tested by leaving one family out. Two applied reviews, in clinical artificial intelligence and in genetic cardiomyopathy, demonstrate it: non-database streams supplied 60–64% of the core corpora, most key findings were robust across three or more families, and a database-only design would have missed two to three findings per review. 360° MDL complements PRISMA and offers authors, editors and assessors an auditable route from evidence volume to tested synthesis.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract    Background and aims.  Diabetic Foot Syndrome (DFS) is a serious complication of diabetes, increasing mortality and cardiovascular risk. Although artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in medicine, few studies have applied Machine Learning (ML) models combining clinical variables with cardiovascular, inflammatory, genetic and epigenetic markers in DFS. This study aimed to develop and internally validate ML models predicting major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in patients with type 2 diabetes with and without DFS, with hospitalisation as a secondary outcome, and to identify the variables most associated with MACE.  Methods.  This retrospective analysis used the database of a single-centre observational cohort of 40 patients with type 2 diabetes and DFS and 40 age- and sex-matched diabetic controls without foot ulcers, enrolled in 2014–2015 and followed for at least 8 years. We analyzed clinical, cardiovascular (PWV, RHI, LF/HF), adipo-inflammation (Omentin-1, Gremlin-1, VEGF, HIF-1α), epigenetic (miR-217-5p, miR-503-5p) and genetic (VEGF − 2578 C > A polymorphism) markers. Logistic Regression and Random Forest models were developed to predict MACE (non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal ischaemic stroke and all-cause death) and internally validated with stratified 5-fold cross-validation; no external validation was performed.  Results.  DFS was associated with higher odds of MACE (OR 2.71, 95% CI 1.05–7.00; p = 0.039). ML models showed moderate predictive performance (Random Forest AUC: 0.78, 95% CI 0.68–0.88), achieving maximal sensitivity through decision threshold recalibration. Key predictors identified included antiplatelet therapy, LF/HF ratio, VEGF levels, PWV, and endothelial function. In exploratory univariate analyses, patients with MACE had higher PWV, LF/HF and Gremlin-1 and lower VEGF (p Conclusions.  In patients with type 2 diabetes, DFS was associated with higher odds of MACE over at least 8 years. An exploratory model combining conventional risk factors, vascular and autonomic indices (PWV, LF/HF) and circulating biomarkers (VEGF, Gremlin-1) showed moderate discrimination at internal validation, with no advantage of Random Forest over Logistic Regression. These findings highlight the importance of comprehensive cardiovascular assessment and aggressive risk factor management in DFS patients, while supporting the potential role of ML in clinical decision-making. These hypothesis-generating findings require confirmation in larger cohorts with external validation.

In Escherichia coli and Saccharomyces cerevisiae long-term evolution data, fixed, essential-gene, and recurrent mutations carry elevated kGain values that grow more pronounced over successive generati…
papers.abstract_full: Current approaches to variant effect prediction center on protein function and interspecies conservation, largely ignoring cues embedded in local nucleotide composition. We developed kGain, a metric that quantifies how a point mutation reshapes oligonucleotide frequency relative to the host genome. In Escherichia coli and Saccharomyces cerevisiae long-term evolution data, fixed, essential-gene, and recurrent mutations carry elevated kGain values that grow more pronounced over successive generations. Parallel trends appear in SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern and in a bottleneck resistance experiment, where a high-kGain fusA Y515N change conferred antibiotic resistance at no detectable fitness cost. A transformer regressor trained on one strain transfers accurately to others, indicating that the compositional rules kGain captures are broadly conserved and offering a new sequence-intrinsic dimension for understanding adaptive selection.

papers.abstract_full: GENE TARGET is a previously published framework designed to quantitatively assess the suitability of a specific monogenic neurodevelopment disorder (NDD) for development of genetic therapies, addressing the need for a systematic and rigorous approach to research prioritization and resource allocation. Here, to keep pace with the rapidly evolving knowledgebase, we refined the framework with more nuanced scoring definitions and added a resource guide to standardize evaluation of each criterion. Interrater agreement was assessed and found to be substantial for most domain/criteria scores among experienced users, primarily genetic counselors with at least two years of experience in translational genomic medicine. Secondary scoring adjudication by experts with clinical/molecular genetics and preclinical modeling expertise is recommended. Cross-disorder analysis of 57 NDD gene-disorder pairs evaluated at the Translational Neuroscience Center was performed, which identified clinical considerations, including establishing endpoints, as the most common translational research gap. Common barriers across disorders also included generating natural history data, establishing an early diagnosis, understanding dosage sensitivity, and demonstrating phenotypic reversibility. We further discuss application of this framework for gene editing and small molecules approaches. Future goals include the validation of GENE TARGET beyond academic research settings and the use of artificial intelligence to aid in preliminary scoring.

papers.title: Probiotics and Prebiotics in Restoring Gastrointestinal Microbiota Dysbiosis: Emerging Alternatives to Antibiotic Therapy.
papers.abstract: The human gastrointestinal (GI) microbiota is a complex and dynamic microbial ecosystem that plays a fundamental role in maintaining host metabolism, immune homeostasis, intestinal barrier integrity, and protection against pathogenic microorganisms. Disruption of this microbial community, known as gut dysbiosis, has been implicated in the pathogenesis of numerous GI and systemic diseases, including inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), Clostridioides difficile infecti…
papers.abstract_full: The human gastrointestinal (GI) microbiota is a complex and dynamic microbial ecosystem that plays a fundamental role in maintaining host metabolism, immune homeostasis, intestinal barrier integrity, and protection against pathogenic microorganisms. Disruption of this microbial community, known as gut dysbiosis, has been implicated in the pathogenesis of numerous GI and systemic diseases, including inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), Clostridioides difficile infection, obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus, colorectal cancer, and nonalcoholic fatty liver disease. Although antibiotics remain indispensable for the treatment of bacterial infections, their indiscriminate use frequently disrupts gut microbial composition, reduces microbial diversity, promotes opportunistic pathogen overgrowth, and accelerates the emergence of antimicrobial resistance. These limitations have stimulated increasing interest in microbiota-targeted interventions as safer and more sustainable therapeutic strategies. Probiotics and prebiotics have emerged as promising approaches for restoring gut microbial homeostasis through complementary mechanisms. Probiotics inhibit pathogen colonization, enhance intestinal barrier function, produce antimicrobial metabolites, and modulate host immune responses. Prebiotics selectively stimulate the growth and metabolic activity of beneficial microorganisms, promoting the production of short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) that support intestinal and systemic health. Increasing evidence from experimental studies, randomized clinical trials, and meta-analyses demonstrates that these microbiota-directed interventions can reduce antibiotic-associated diarrhea, improve symptoms of IBD and IBS, enhance Helicobacter pylori eradication, decrease recurrence of C. difficile infection, and contribute to the management of several metabolic disorders. Despite these promising findings, important challenges remain regarding strain specificity, optimal dosage, treatment duration, product standardization, regulatory oversight, and interindividual variability in treatment response. Emerging advances in metagenomics, metabolomics, artificial intelligence, and precision medicine are facilitating the development of personalized microbiome-based therapies that may further enhance clinical outcomes. This review critically summarizes the current understanding of GI microbiota dysbiosis, discusses the mechanisms through which probiotics and prebiotics restore microbial balance, evaluates their clinical applications as alternatives or adjuncts to antibiotic therapy, and highlights existing challenges and future research directions for microbiome-based therapeutics.

papers.abstract: Recent advances in precision oncology fueled the development of nanotherapeutics,​ molecularly targeted drugs, engineered immunotherapies, RNA therapeutics, and smart biomaterials for more selective cancer treatment. papers.abstract_full: Recent advances in precision oncology fueled the development of nanotherapeutics,​ molecularly targeted drugs, engineered immunotherapies, RNA therapeutics, and smart biomaterials for more selective cancer treatment. However, long-term therapeutic responses remain restricted by interconnected adaptive mechanisms, including ABC transporter-mediated drug efflux, dysregulated signaling pathways, apoptosis evasion, immune escape, epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, and tumor microenvironment​ remodeling. In this review article, these processes are collectively framed as tumor-mediated molecular hijacking, describing malignant cell exploitation and microenvironmental pathways that promote multidrug resistance and therapeutic failure. The review critically examines nanotherapeutic and advanced biotherapeutic strategies to counteract these mechanisms, including functionalized nanocarriers, antibody-drug conjugates, CAR-T cells, tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte therapy, immune checkpoint blockade, mesenchymal stem-cell (MSC)-based therapeutics, CRISPR-mediated genome editing, bispecific T-cell engagers, and RNA-based approaches. Particular focus includes drug-delivery elements such as tumour penetration, intracellular trafficking, controlled release, pharmacokinetics, biodistribution, and critical formulation attributes, as well as translational challenges such as manufacturability, scalability, reproducibility, stability, safety, and regulatory feasibility. Emerging biofabrication approaches enable the fabrication of adaptive and personalized delivery systems, while artificial intelligence and machine learning are utilized as tools for structure-guided design, nanocarrier optimization, treatment-response prediction, and patient-specific digital-twin modelling. This paper combines tumor-mediated molecular hijacking with drug delivery technology at the forefront and translational aspects to create a comprehensive platform for clinically relevant precision cancer therapeutics.Clinical trial number: Not applicable.

Growth, stabilization, and disintegration were labeled according to consecutive-day changes in median particle diameter (ΔD50). Agreement between expert consensus and thr…
papers.abstract_full: Reliable identification of aerobic granular sludge (AGS) granulation stages can support cultivation monitoring and operational adjustment. We collected 231 microscopic images and particle size measurements from three sequencing batch reactors operated at influent chemical oxygen demand concentrations of 250, 500, and 1000 mg/L. Growth, stabilization, and disintegration were labeled according to consecutive-day changes in median particle diameter (ΔD50). Agreement between expert consensus and threshold-based labels was 88.31% (Cohen's κ = 0.823). Fractal dimension (FD) was calculated by box counting at 20, 40, and 80 pixels to characterize two-dimensional spatial occupancy of sludge foreground. Conventional machine learning, numerical-feature, image-only, image-numerical fusion, and vision-language models were compared. Trained models were evaluated using leave-one-reactor-out cross-validation across five training runs, with an 80:20 training-validation split in the two remaining reactors. FD was higher and less variable during stabilization (1.644 ± 0.082) than during growth (1.587 ± 0.087) or disintegration (1.580 ± 0.114). Adding FD increased the macro-averaged F1 score of ResNet34 from 0.866 to 0.905 and reduced confusion between stabilization and disintegration. ResNet34FD-Gated achieved the highest mean accuracy (0.919 ± 0.012) and Macro-F1 (0.920 ± 0.012). Input permutation analysis identified microscopic images as the dominant information source for stage classification. Integrating FD with microscopic images and particle size improved stage identification under laboratory conditions, although external validation remains necessary.

papers.abstract_full: Classifying viral pathogens from next-generation sequencing (NGS) data is central to diagnosis and genomic surveillance. Most deep learning classifiers, however, read only a fixed window at the start of each genome, typically a few hundred to a few thousand base pairs, and so ignore more than 95% of the sequence of large DNA viruses such as monkeypox virus (MPV) and herpes simplex virus 1 (HSV-1). We refer to this problem as Truncation Blindness. Here we present Viro-BERT, which splits a complete genome into overlapping 512-token windows, encodes each window with a shared DistilBERT encoder, and averages the window-level class probabilities in a Late Fusion Consensus layer. Because the windows are processed independently, memory use does not grow with genome length. We compared Viro-BERT with one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN), bidirectional long short-term memory (Bi-LSTM) and RoBERTa baselines on 14 viral classes, using the same segmentation and training protocol for all models. Viro-BERT reached 96.79% accuracy and a macro-F1 score of 96.17%. We then added random substitution noise to the test genomes. At 5% noise, the accuracy of the 1D-CNN fell by 5.57 percentage points, whereas Viro-BERT still classified 93.68% of genomes correctly. Positional and attention analyses on HSV-1 showed that Viro-BERT uses diagnostic signal from across the genome rather than from its 5' end alone. These results indicate that whole-genome context is needed for viral classifiers that remain reliable on noisy clinical data.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Microplastics (MPs) and their toxic components (BPA, DBP, DEHP) pose global health threats, with the liver as primary target. The mechanisms by which MPs may contribute to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) progression and spatial microenvironment remodeling remain poorly understood. METHODS: We employed an integrated multi-omics workflow combining bulk transcriptomics, WGCNA, ten machine learning algorithms combined into 101 candidate model combinations, single-cell RNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics (ST), inferCNV, CytoTRACE, and molecular docking with 100 ns molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. RESULTS: We identified 22 hub genes at the putative intersection of HCC dysregulation and documented toxicological targets of MP-associated chemicals (BPA, DBP, and DEHP), enriched in cell cycle and senescence. A 6-gene (AKR1C3, AURKA, CCNB1, EZH2, FABP5, ESR1) risk model (glmBoost + SVM) achieved high diagnostic accuracy (mean external AUC = 0.965; internal bootstrap validation of the six-gene logistic model: bias-corrected AUC = 0.987 (optimism = 0.005). papers.abstract_full: Vascular dementia (VaD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by chronic cerebral hypoperfusion and cognitive decline, yet the role of fatty acid metabolism in its pathogenesis remains incompletely understood. Integrated transcriptomic profiling was combined with network-based analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) and machine learning to uncover key fatty acid metabolism-associated molecular features associated with VaD. Single-cell RNA sequencing, intercellular communication inference, and in silico perturbation analyses were applied to define immune-stromal interactions. Potential therapeutic compounds were evaluated using molecular docking and dynamics simulations. We identified three VaD-related fatty acid metabolism genes (VaD-FAMRGs), namely PNPLA3, HSP90AA1, and ALB, which showed consistent diagnostic performance across multiple computational approaches and were associated with lipid metabolism, inflammatory processes, and neurovascular unit dysfunction. Functional enrichment, single-cell RNA sequencing, and in silico gene perturbation analyses provided exploratory insights into the potential associations of these candidate genes with lipid transport, metabolic regulation, synaptic maintenance, and immune-inflammatory processes. Cell-cell communication analysis further revealed activation of the ANGPTL signaling axis, suggesting impaired endothelial-glial interactions driven by lipid metabolic dysregulation. Regulatory network analysis identified key transcriptional and post-transcriptional regulators, including REST, miR-155-5p, and miR-21-5p, which may coordinately modulate VaD-FAMRG expression. Drug repurposing analysis highlighted quercetin as a candidate compound with predicted interactions with all three hub proteins, supported by molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations. These findings suggest that dysregulated fatty acid metabolism may be associated with the development and progression of VaD through coordinated metabolic, inflammatory, and neurovascular mechanisms. This study provides a systems-level framework for understanding the underlying pathological processes and establishes a theoretical basis for future mechanistic and experimental validation.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Fulvestrant serves as cornerstone endocrine therapy for hormone receptor-positive (HR-positive) advanced breast cancer. Recent reports indicate safety concerns regarding respiratory toxicity. This study systematically characterized fulvestrant-related respiratory adverse events (adverse events, AEs) using two independent spontaneous reporting databases (FAERS and JADER) for cross-verification and investigated underlying mechanisms. METHODS: Disproportionality analysis utilized two post-marketing surveillance databases, the United States Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) and Japanese Adverse Drug Event Report (JADER), applying reporting odds ratio (ROR) and Bayesian confidence propagation neural network (BCPNN) methods for respiratory adverse event signal detection. Fulvestrant targets were predicted using SwissTargetPrediction, TargetNet, and Therapeutic Target Database (TTD). Lung disease-related genes were identified from GeneCards and Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man (OMIM). Overlapping targets underwent Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analysis. A protein-protein interaction (PPI) network was constructed with STRING and Cytoscape, core genes identified by maximum clique centrality (MCC) algorithm. CB-Dock2 platform performed molecular docking between fulvestrant and key targets. RESULTS: A total of 6988 fulvestrant-related reports were included from FAERS with 896 respiratory toxicity cases, while 1582 fulvestrant-associated adverse event reports were retrieved from JADER, covering 154 respiratory toxicity cases. Twenty-two respiratory adverse event signals were detected in FAERS, among which nine consistent positive signals were replicated in JADER, including pleural effusion (ROR = 5.38), interstitial lung disease (ROR = 3.94), and dyspnea (ROR = 1.50). Median time to onset was 70 days (interquartile range 21-227 days). Network pharmacology analysis identified 78 overlapping targets between fulvestrant and lung diseases. Enrichment analysis indicated involvement of inflammatory response, immune regulation, oxidative stress pathways, tumor necrosis factor (TNF) signaling pathway, and interleukin 17 (IL-17) signaling pathway. Molecular docking suggested favorable predicted binding conformations between fulvestrant and several core proteins, including mitogen-activated protein kinase 14 (MAPK14), hypoxia inducible factor 1 subunit alpha (HIF1A), and mitogen-activated protein kinase 1 (MAPK1), although these findings remain computational and require further validation. CONCLUSION: This hypothesis-generating integrated dual-database pharmacovigilance and network pharmacology analysis revealed significant association between fulvestrant and multiple respiratory toxicities, often occurring early during treatment. Potential mechanisms may involve inflammatory response, immune dysregulation, and oxidative stress-related pathways. The molecular docking findings provide exploratory computational support only and do not constitute direct evidence of in vivo interactions or causal mechanisms. Cross-database validation greatly improved the robustness of our analytical results, yet definite causality still cannot be established due to inherent limitations of spontaneous reporting systems. These findings require external validation and experimental verification and provide theoretical basis for clinical risk management and further mechanistic research.

papers.abstract: Cell competition is a conserved fitness-surveillance process, first described in Drosophila epithelia, by which cells compare relative fitness with their neighbors so that less-fit "loser" cells are eliminated, extruded or forced to differentiate while fitter "winner" cells expand. papers.abstract_full: Cell competition is a conserved fitness-surveillance process, first described in Drosophila epithelia, by which cells compare relative fitness with their neighbors so that less-fit "loser" cells are eliminated, extruded or forced to differentiate while fitter "winner" cells expand. In the tumor microenvironment (TME), this logic appears to be co-opted by transformed clones that eliminate normal epithelium, outcompete neighboring subclones and reshape stromal and immune compartments, making cell competition a potentially underappreciated contributor to cancer clonal evolution, immune escape and therapy resistance. Because competition is defined by a comparison between adjacent cells and by a demonstrated change in the relative representation of one population, it is difficult to resolve with bulk sequencing, which averages across precisely the heterogeneity that defines it. The convergence of single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), spatial transcriptomics, spatial and single-cell proteomics, artificial intelligence (AI) and network-inference bioinformatics now allows competition-relevant cellular states, interfaces and signaling relationships to be measured at the resolution the problem requires. We emphasize at the outset that these technologies are, in almost all current applications, hypothesis-generating: they identify candidate competitive interfaces and putative winner and loser states from static measurements, and they do not by themselves demonstrate that competition has occurred. This review synthesizes advances across these domains; proposes an explicit three-tier evidence framework separating direct experimental evidence of cell competition from competition-relevant associations and from computational predictions; distinguishes cell competition from related processes such as clonal selection, immune editing and differential proliferation; and defines a putative cell competition network as a falsifiable construct whose edges include ligand-receptor, spatial-adjacency, metabolic and mechanical relations. We further outline a conceptual, context-dependent Cell Competition Score (CCS) as a testable specification rather than a biomarker-ready instrument, and set out the benchmarking, causal-inference and prospective-validation requirements that stand between current capability and any clinical application.

papers.abstract_full: Background/Objectives: Dietary compounds simultaneously act on host tissue and gut microbiota, complicating efforts to distinguish direct host-receptor mechanisms from microbiome-mediated effects. Using a common food ingredient as proof-of-principle, this study aims to disentangle capsaicin host receptor signalling from capsaicin-microbiome interactions to determine the role of the gut microbiome in capsaicin-mediated metabolic protection. Methods: We employed a high-fat diet (HFD)-induced obesity model with or without capsaicin supplementation in TRPV1 knockout mice to determine the role of the host receptor. We also depleted the gut microbiota with antibiotics to determine the role of the microbiome. Host metabolic phenotypes were monitored, and microbiome 16S rRNA sequencing and metabolomics were analysed and extended with functional prediction and machine learning algorithms, followed by functional validation in vivo. Results: Capsaicin supplementation significantly protected against HFD-induced obesity, even capsaicin receptor knockout hosts. Crucially, depletion of the microbiota abolished this metabolic protection, demonstrating the microbiome's obligatory role. While capsaicin supplementation did not alter hosts' cumulative food intake, dietary preferences, or energy expenditure, it induced significant shifts in gut microbial diversity and function and triggered extensive faecal metabolomic remodelling which indicate altered nutrient processing including dampened lipid absorption. Consistent with this finding, in vivo functional validation also reveals attenuated circulating lipid response following oral fat administration, and this effect of capsaicin is abrogated without the microbiome. Conclusions: Although capsaicin is well-recognised as a modulator of host appetite and metabolism via canonical host receptor signalling, our strategic use of a host knockout has enabled us to unmask a nuanced microbiome-modulatory role of this chilli pepper ingredient: capsaicin tweaks the microbiome to potentially dial down host fat absorption and protect against high-fat diet-induced obesity. We also highlight a generalisable host knockout experimental framework for distinguishing microbiome-mediated pathways versus direct host receptor mechanisms.

papers.abstract_full: As the primary cash crop for natural fiber, cotton develops under sophisticated endogenous genetic programs, with biotic and abiotic stresses continuously driving its adaptive evolution. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are post-transcriptional regulators that modulate gene expression via target mRNA cleavage, translational repression, and mediation of DNA methylation. miRNAs target transcription factors and hormone signaling pathways to regulate cotton plant architecture and fiber development. In addition, miRNAs mitigate biotic and abiotic stresses through ROS, lignin, and hormone pathways, as well as by forming competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) modules with long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs). This review establishes an miRNA-centered regulatory framework that coordinates cotton growth, development, and stress resistance. A series of technologies, including multi-omics combined with machine learning, gene overexpression, STTM, MIM, MIGS, CRISPR editing, foliar dsRNA spraying, and bionanocarriers, are proposed to facilitate the breeding of cotton varieties with high yield, superior fiber quality, and broad-spectrum stress tolerance.

papers.abstract_full: Autoimmune encephalitis (AE) and paraneoplastic neurological syndromes (PNS) are leading causes of potentially reversible but frequently misdiagnosed neurological disability, and delayed recognition worsens outcomes and impedes timely tumor detection. This narrative review is written from a laboratory medicine perspective and focuses on the analytical determinants of early and accurate diagnosis: appropriate test selection, dual-method confirmation combining tissue-based and cell-based assays, phenotype-guided interpretation, and assay harmonization. We summarize the expanding spectrum of neuronal and glial autoantibodies, quantitative biomarkers of neuroaxonal injury-most notably neurofilament light chain-and investigational cerebrospinal fluid markers, including cytokine profiles, kappa free light chains, and markers of astrocytic injury, whose ability to discriminate AE from infectious mimics has not been established. We highlight novel autoantibody discovery through phage immunoprecipitation sequencing, research-stage multi-omics approaches, and early, retrospectively evaluated artificial intelligence-assisted classifiers, and we address the growing challenge of neurological adverse events triggered by immune checkpoint inhibitors. Priorities for translation into routine care include external quality assurance, certified reference materials, age-adjusted reference intervals, and prospective validation of integrated biomarker panels within reference-center networks. The review provides a structured framework to support precision laboratory diagnostics in neuroimmunology.

papers.abstract_full: Premise: Polyploidy is a persistent feature of land plant evolution, yet it is often difficult to determine the ploidy of individual plants. The growing abundance of target capture data and other high-throughput sequence datasets across plant species has generated interest in methods to infer ploidy from these data. We leverage chromosome count data and target capture data from the GoFlag probe set in ferns to train new machine learning models to infer if a sample is from a diploid or polyploid genome. Methods and Results: We trained a convolutional neural network (CNN) for each GoFlag probe locus and developed ensemble models that use two loci and a random forest model that leverages all the loci to classify fern samples as diploid or polyploid. We tested the performance of these models using held-out test datasets of GoFlag target capture data across ferns and an independent test set from the genus Lygodium. We also performed experiments to evaluate the features of loci and sequences most associated with model performance and tested the performance of the models as sequence depth decreased. Conclusions: These models, collectively named sorAI, outperform the frequency-based methods nQuire and nQuack on held-out test datasets of GoFlag target capture data across ferns. These models are capable of leveraging positional information and covariation among nucleotide sites beyond individual-site allele frequencies, and they perform well even with low sequence coverage. The random forest model, which uses all loci, appears to be robust to varying dataset features and achieves an accuracy of approximately 71-78% across test datasets and sequencing depths. sorAI is available at https://github.com/Fahimehgit/sorai, and the trained models are available at https://huggingface.co/Fahimehr140/sorai.

papers.abstract: Pathogen genomic surveillance works from raw reads, assembled genomes and alignments, representations that are slow and costly to compare at scale. Compact embeddings from genomic language models offer an alternative, but surveillance requires resolving both evolutionary ancestry (phylogeny) and phenotypic capability (function) - which need not co-vary. papers.abstract_full: Pathogen genomic surveillance works from raw reads, assembled genomes and alignments, representations that are slow and costly to compare at scale. Compact embeddings from genomic language models offer an alternative, but surveillance requires resolving both evolutionary ancestry (phylogeny) and phenotypic capability (function) - which need not co-vary. Here we present MicroDUET, which adapts a 26.6-million-parameter ProkBERT backbone with two 3.5-million-parameter adapter heads: a phylogeny head trained contrastively on genome windows from the same microbes, and a function head trained to identify genes across taxa. On held-out retrieval benchmarks, the phylogeny head returned the correct species for 80.3% and 66.6% of cellular and viral queries, and the function head the correct gene family for 97.3% and 97.2%, reaching 74.4% accuracy on an independent antimicrobial resistance-class benchmark. Across all three benchmarks MicroDUET outranked 17 other genomic encoders. Without training on lineage, clade or drug-susceptibility tasks, MicroDUET identified Mycobacterium tuberculosis and mpox virus lineages and clades (0.965, 0.975 accuracy), discriminated rifampicin resistance without lineage adjustment (AUROC 0.985), and retrospectively identified an emerging mpox lineage as anomalous (AUROC 0.974). MicroDUET operates 10^3 - 10^4 times faster than single-threaded sequence-based alignments. MicroDUET therefore provides a compact, reusable representation for scalable pathogen surveillance and sequence triage.

papers.abstract_full: Multimodal genomic datasets now profile mammalian brain cells across anatomical regions, developmental stages, disease states, and species. Learning shared representations that capture cellular diversity across these heterogeneous observations remains a central challenge. Here, we introduce Bloom, a transformer-based model that represents cells using gene expression, chromatin accessibility, or both. Bloom is trained on 300,000 adult mouse brain cells with paired measurements, randomly sampled with broad-subclass balancing—approximately 100-fold fewer cells than used by comparable pre-trained models. By combining genomic sequence embeddings with randomly sampled multimodal cell views, Bloom outperforms unimodal cell models in resolving brain-wide cell types and in annotation, regression, and label-transfer tasks. Its attention patterns reveal cell-type-dependent associations among genomic loci, including pairs separated by millions of base pairs. These results establish Bloom as a data-efficient framework for integrating multimodal brain cell measurements and generating hypotheses about cell-type-specific genomic relationships.

papers.abstract: Multicellular organisms develop and maintain differentiated cell states through a combination of cell-autonomous and non-autonomous regulatory mechanisms, including signal transduction pathways mediated by ligands, receptors, and kinases. papers.abstract_full: Multicellular organisms develop and maintain differentiated cell states through a combination of cell-autonomous and non-autonomous regulatory mechanisms, including signal transduction pathways mediated by ligands, receptors, and kinases. Genetic perturbation through CRISPR pooled screening is widely used to study cell-autonomous regulatory mechanisms, but the challenges of cellular-resolution in situ measurement have limited the study of non-autonomous regulatory mechanisms. We developed Perturb-Tags, a spatial multi-omic technique for pooled CRISPR screening that tags nuclei with spatial barcodes, allowing joint measurement of single-nucleus gene expression, CRISPR guide RNAs, chromatin accessibility, and spatial positions within intact tissue. Perturb-Tags achieves cellular-resolution, unbiased gene expression and multi-omic profiling, and higher sensitivity than previous spatial perturbation approaches. We used Perturb-Tags to systematically perturb ligands, receptors, and all expressed kinases in human embryoid bodies. These experiments revealed extensive non-autonomous gene expression changes after perturbation, including distance-dependent loss of signaling pathway activity upon ligand knockdown, compensatory upregulation of alternative signaling pathways, and responses to receptor and kinase knockdown that vary with cell microenvironment. We also identified changes in the spatial organization of cells with ligand and kinase knockdowns. Finally, we trained a graph neural network to model the combined effects of genetic perturbations on gene expression and chromatin accessibility across an entire tissue. Our work provides a powerful experimental and computational platform for mechanistic studies of non-autonomous regulatory mechanisms across healthy and diseased tissues.

papers.abstract: Small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) silence target genes through RISC-mediated hybridization and cleavage, but can silence unintended transcripts and cause toxicity or complicate regulatory approval. papers.abstract_full: Small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) silence target genes through RISC-mediated hybridization and cleavage, but can silence unintended transcripts and cause toxicity or complicate regulatory approval. In drug development, empirical assessment by qPCR and RNA-seq is slow, forces early candidate prioritization, and is limited by available species- and genome-appropriate cell models. While extensive empirical screening remains standard practice, there is a significant opportunity for modern AI methods to change this paradigm. We introduce DeepRNAi, a deep learning model that accurately predicts on- and off-target knockdown from siRNA and mRNA sequence. Trained on 16 million siRNA-transcript pairs from 2,031 siRNAs designed to interrogate known siRNA failure modes, and incorporating transcript context from biological foundation models, DeepRNAi is the first in silico method that approaches experimental accuracy. It generalizes across cell models, transcripts, genomes and species, and in a small study distinguishes approved therapeutics from hepatotoxic candidates. The value of DeepRNAi for prioritizing better candidates up front improving likelihood of success later in development is evidenced by a genome-wide survey of 24.4 million siRNAs targeting 7,946 genes, which indicates that 90.1% of the 100 most potent siRNAs have at least some off-target concerns. To support the community, we are publishing a training and benchmark dataset containing 1.84 million siRNA-transcript pairs from 240 siRNAs.

papers.abstract_full: Influenza A virus (IAV) populations are characterized by a high prevalence of non-infectious virions, with particle-to-plaque forming unit (PFU) ratios typically ranging from 10 to 1,000. While "multiplicity reactivation" -the process by which incomplete viral genomes (IVGs) establish productive infection through co-infection- has long been hypothesized, its quantitative nature has remained elusive. In this study, we utilized a digital influenza assay to achieve absolute quantification of IAV particles, allowing us to define the particle-based multiplicity of infection (pMOI) for precise evaluation. We combined this approach with a single-cell infection assay using microcompartmentalized containers and machine learning-based automated cell classification to accurately assess infection outcomes across a wide range of pMOIs. Our analysis of the A/Puerto Rico/8/1934 (H1N1) revealed a count-to-plaque forming unit (PFU) ratio of approximately 400, meaning only a tiny fraction of particles possesses infectivity. Remarkably, the infection rate in single-cell infection experiments followed a sigmoidal curve and reached saturation at a pMOI of only 5 to 10. This demonstrates that under high-pMOI conditions, productive infection is predominantly driven by genome complementation among incomplete particles rather than solely by fully infectious virions. On the other hand, mathematical model analysis based on these findings suggested that the functionality of each of the eight genomic segments within a virus particle follows a stochastic process, resulting in a probability distribution for the number of functional segments per particle. This mechanism proved exceptionally robust across multiple strains despite a 20-fold variation in CTPR values. Ultimately, these findings indicate that incomplete particles are not merely biological noise but active contributors to the infection process, significantly enhancing the infectivity and evolutionary flexibility of IAV. This study will provide a more refined understanding of influenza transmission dynamics and risk assessment, particularly in environments where multiple virus particles are present within a single respiratory droplet.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract    Wasabi's high market value drives its adulteration with taxonomically related analogues, compromising food quality and safety. We developed an integrated approach combining chloroplast genome comparison, DNA barcoding with machine learning classifiers, and nutritional profiling to distinguish wasabi from adulterants. Among seven Brassicaceae species, chloroplast genomes were largely conserved but exhibited species-specific variations in IR boundaries, SSRs, hypervariable regions, and weak A/U-ended codon bias. Of three barcodes (ITS2,  matK  ,  rbcL  ), ITS2 showed the clearest barcoding gap and best phylogenetic resolution, while machine learning (BLOG and WEKA) identified  matK  as the top marker with 100% accuracy. Nutritional analysis revealed significant differences in flavonoids, polyphenols, and vitamin C across species. This framework offers a robust authenticity solution integrating genomic, molecular, and nutritional data.

papers.title: Precision Oncology and Regenerative Strategies in Esophageal Cancer: From Tumor Cell Plasticity and Microenvironmental Networks to Functional Models and Tissue Repair
papers.abstract: Esophageal cancer (EC), comprising esophageal squamous cell carcinoma and esophageal adenocarcinoma, remains a highly aggressive malignancy characterized by substantial intratumoral heterogeneity, cellular plasticity, therapeutic resistance, and poor clinical outcomes. Increasing evidence indicates that EC progression is governed not only by tumor-intrinsic genetic alterations but also by dynamic interactions among signaling networks, metabolic and epigenetic programs, cancer stem-like states, s…
papers.abstract_full: Esophageal cancer (EC), comprising esophageal squamous cell carcinoma and esophageal adenocarcinoma, remains a highly aggressive malignancy characterized by substantial intratumoral heterogeneity, cellular plasticity, therapeutic resistance, and poor clinical outcomes. Increasing evidence indicates that EC progression is governed not only by tumor-intrinsic genetic alterations but also by dynamic interactions among signaling networks, metabolic and epigenetic programs, cancer stem-like states, stromal and immune cells, extracellular matrix, vasculature, neural components, and the microbiome. In this review, we synthesize advances in the cellular and molecular biology of EC and discuss their implications for precision therapeutic strategies, with emphasis on oncogenic signaling, pathway rewiring, tumor–microenvironment interactions, cancer stem-cell plasticity, and emerging biomarker platforms, including multi-omics, liquid biopsy, extracellular vesicles, single-cell sequencing, and spatial transcriptomics. We further examine patient-derived organoids, organoid–immune co-culture systems, three-dimensional bioprinted tumor models, and computational approaches as functional platforms for investigating tumor heterogeneity, therapeutic response, and treatment resistance. Beyond tumor control, tissue-engineering and regenerative strategies for repairing treatment-associated mucosal injury, fibrosis, stricture, and tissue loss are discussed. Importantly, regenerative interventions require careful oncologic consideration because pathways involved in tissue repair, stem-cell activation, angiogenesis, and extracellular-matrix remodeling may influence residual malignant cells. Finally, we highlight the convergence of precision oncology, functional tumor modeling, regenerative medicine, and artificial intelligence, while addressing challenges in standardization, validation, scalability, regulation, and clinical translation.

papers.abstract_full: Combined sewer systems can discharge untreated combined sewer overflows (CSOs) during intense rainfall, while conventional storage tunnels require substantial capital investment and may disrupt urban traffic during construction. This study proposes an integrated modernization framework combining Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II)-based placement of roadside bioretention cells with real-time gate and pump control driven by a physics-informed machine-learning (PIML) surrogate. The surrogate incorporates the one-dimensional Saint-Venant mass- and momentum-conservation equations into its training objective. The framework was evaluated using an EPA SWMM 5.2-based benchmark catchment under 1-, 2-, 5-, and 10-year synthetic design storms. Against the supplied SWMM benchmark outputs, the PIML surrogate achieved a Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency (NSE) of 0.952 and a reported inference latency of 0.32 ms, compared with a mean SWMM runtime of 14.5 min. The integrated scenario reduced peak runoff from 48.2 to 19.6 m³/s (59.3%) and increased reported storage utilization from 42.0% to 94.5%. Simulated CSO discharge was reduced to zero for the 1-, 2-, and 5-year storms and from 210,000 to 12,400 m³ for the 10-year storm (94.1%). Road-waterlogging duration decreased from 4.2 to 0.3 h (92.9%). Using the cost components stated in the manuscript, baseline capital cost is $250 million and proposed capital cost is $20 million, corresponding to an estimated 92.0% reduction; regulatory penalties are excluded from capital expenditure. These are model-based estimates and require reproducible model files, cost documentation, and field validation before practical deployment.

papers.abstract: Summary:  Identifying epigenetically modified bases (e.g., methylation) is crucial for many important applications such as discovering mechanisms of cancer development, cell differentiation, and bacterial defense. papers.abstract_full: Summary:  Identifying epigenetically modified bases (e.g., methylation) is crucial for many important applications such as discovering mechanisms of cancer development, cell differentiation, and bacterial defense. Nanopore sequencing generates electrical signals that can differentiate canonical bases from modified ones. To detect base modifications from signals, machine learning (ML) methods and statistical approaches are commonly used. These methods can either detect a specific modification type or require an additional unmodified copy of the same DNA as a control group. However, no released model detects modification types beyond those it was trained for, which makes it difficult to detect rare modification types without an unmodified control. Our goal is to accurately identify the presence of modified sites regardless of their modification type, which we define as modification-agnostic detection. To this end, we propose RawMod, a transformer-based modification-agnostic and control-free method for detecting epigenetically modified genomic positions. The key idea of RawMod is to compare the raw signals of many reads at each site with the unmodified reference sequence, using a small model that learns many modification types as a single modified class. Based on our extensive evaluations on the detection of various modification types (5mC, 5hmC, 4mC, 6mA, and 5hmU) using various genomes, RawMod achieves the highest mean AUROC across modifications compared to control-based methods and control-free modification models. A single RawMod model with 0.23M parameters detects five modification types with a mean AUROC of 0.964, against 0.799 for the best released model. When a modification type is withheld from training, RawMod still detects it (AUROC 0.91—0.98), provided another modification of the same base was seen in training.  We use RawMod to map 5hmU without a control across a 7.7 Mb contig of the Amphidinium carterae genome, consistent with two published trends. Further, we show that the modification-aware embeddings from RawMod can be used to differentiate read origin (e.g., cell types, tumor/normal origin, and native/PCR-amplified DNA). We discuss how RawMod can enable further work on label-free classification of cell types using these modification-aware embeddings.  Availability and Implementation: RawMod is available at https://github.com/STORMgroup/RawMod and at https://huggingface.co/STORMResearch/RawMod. We also provide the scripts to fully reproduce our results on our GitHub page and release our datasets on SquiDBase.

papers.abstract: The central nervous system (CNS) comprises diverse cell types whose molecular context shapes the roles of the proteins they express. papers.abstract_full: The central nervous system (CNS) comprises diverse cell types whose molecular context shapes the roles of the proteins they express. Computational models offer a scalable way to study the roles of proteins across human brain cell types, with protein language models and interactome- or single-cell-based models capturing complementary information encoded in protein sequences and cellular network contexts. Human brain tissue is hard to access, so brain cell types make up a small fraction of the atlases single-cell models train on and of the benchmarks used for their evaluation. To capture these complementary sources of information in the CNS, we introduce SEMPER, a multimodal representation learning model that aligns protein language model representations with protein-protein interaction networks from 442 cell types of the adult human brain, giving each protein a sequence-informed representation in every cell type in which its gene is expressed. We show that SEMPER representations predict cell type-specific protein complexes and predict genes essential to the survival of dopaminergic neurons, measured in a genome-wide CRISPR screen. In zero-shot retrieval, SEMPER recovers clinically pursued drug targets for Parkinson's disease, Alzheimer's disease, multiple sclerosis, Huntington's disease and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis at higher rates than cell type-specific models. To further improve target recovery, we combine SEMPER with a large language model that reasons over protein functional annotations. The combination recovers more targets, with SEMPER providing experimentally derived cellular context that complements literature-based reasoning of the large language model.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract    Clostridium thermocellum  has been extensively studied for its capacity to deconstruct lignocellulose and convert the resulting sugars into ethanol; however, incomplete knowledge of its transcriptional regulatory network (TRN) limits rational strain engineering. Here, we applied independent component analysis (ICA), an unsupervised machine learning approach to a compendium of 223 RNA-seq samples spanning 10 independent studies to systematically resolve transcriptional regulatory structure. The analysis identified 67 independently modulated gene sets called iModulons (IMs) that explain 80.4% of transcriptomic variance to capture regulatory programs. Next, statistical analysis and genome-scale metabolic modeling uncovered a pathway for crosstalk between sulfate assimilation and ethanol production mediated by intracellular redox balance. Finally, comparative analysis across carbon substrates such as cellulose, xylose, and xylan revealed substrate-specific regulatory shifts and candidate control points for improving lignocellulosic sugar utilization. These results provide a systems-wide framework for linking transcriptional regulation to metabolic function and identify actionable targets for engineering  C. thermocellum  for desired phenotype.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning are being applied rapidly across autoimmune neurological disorders, but the overall shape of this literature — which disorders, data modalities and methods dominate, and where evidence is absent — has not been quantified. Objective. To map the published research landscape of AI in autoimmune neurological disorders through a bibliometric analysis, and to identify the field’s concentrations and gaps. Methods. PubMed/MEDLINE was searched in November 2026 using a title/abstract strategy combining terms for autoimmune neurological disorders (multiple sclerosis [MS], NMOSD, MOGAD, autoimmune encephalitis, autoimmune epilepsy, paraneoplastic neurological syndromes) with artificial-intelligence and machine-learning terms, limited to 2015–2026. Records were analysed programmatically for annual output, leading journals, authorship, open-access status, and disorder-, modality- and method-level focus (title-level tagging). Results. 1,455 records were analysed. Annual output rose from 10 (2015) to 270 (2025), with 2026 already at 319 ahead-of-print records; output grew approximately 12-fold between 2015–2018 and 2022– 2025. The literature was dominated by multiple sclerosis (883 records, 60.7%), with all other disorders comparatively rare (NMOSD 45; autoimmune encephalitis 26; MOGAD 11; paraneoplastic 1). MRI was the dominant data modality (517 records, 35.5%), whereas EEG (9), genomics (25) and CSF biomarkers (83) were seldom addressed. Only 33 records (2.3%) described multimodal or data-fusion approaches. Deep learning (259) had overtaken classical machine learning (226). Work was distributed across 463 journals (led by Multiple Sclerosis and Related Disorders, n=84); 63.9% of records were open access. Conclusions. Research on AI in autoimmune neurology is expanding steeply but is heavily concentrated on multiple sclerosis and MRI. Rarer disorders, electrophysiological, fluid-biomarker and genomic data, and genuine multimodal integration remain markedly under-explored — defining clear priorities for future work.

papers.abstract_full: The cryptocurrency market constitutes a complex, non-linear financial ecosystem where traditional econometric frameworks frequently struggle to capture abrupt regime shifts and heavy-tailed crash dynamics. To address this gap, this study synthesizes the application of econophysical signal processing and complexity science in decoding digital asset cycles. Guided by the PRISMA 2020 protocol and a five-domain Risk of Bias (RoB) quality appraisal, this Systematic Literature Review evaluates 30 core empirical and methodological studies (within a 51-source bibliography), establishing a taxonomic classification of time-frequency analysis, adaptive signal decomposition, fractal dynamics, and hybrid machine learning architectures with explicit mathematical formulations and performance benchmarks. The findings indicate that wavelet transforms and Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) isolate non-stationary, multi-scale cyclical behaviors more effectively compared to classical Fourier methods. Furthermore, the temporal evolution of informational complexity metrics—such as Lempel-Ziv Complexity, Bandt-Pompe Permutation Entropy, and Approximate Entropy—reveals pre-crash compression of pattern diversity as a consistent empirical precursor to liquidity evaporation. Additionally, integrating adaptive signal decomposition with hybrid deep learning and α-stable Lévy distributions generally improves forecasting accuracy over standalone linear benchmarks, though regularized parsimonious models (e.g., LASSO and ARIMAX) remain competitive under high noise. Ultimately, non-linear signal engineering provides actionable early warning systems for quantitative asset pricing, latency-aware algorithmic trading, and macroprudential regulatory oversight.

papers.abstract_full: Bryophytes exhibit diverse genome architectures and gene repertoires, yet their functional interpretation remains constrained by incomplete genomic annotations and limited experimental resources. Although DNA foundation models offer promising solutions, their applicability to evolutionarily divergent bryophytes remains largely unexplored. Here, we introduce BryoCAD, a DNA language model developed through continued pre-training of the angiosperm-specific PlantCAD2 model on 17 bryophyte genomes spanning hornworts, liverworts, and mosses. Across three representative bryophyte genomes and four gene-boundary motif recovery tasks, BryoCAD-Small improved mean zero-shot accuracy from 45.7% to 57.0%, a 24.8% relative increase over PlantCAD2-Small, while the over 200-fold larger Evo2-20B achieved a mean accuracy of only 39.3%. Remarkably, BryoCAD-Small outperformed PlantCAD2-Large in 11 of 12 motif-recovery comparisons across the three bryophytes, highlighting the benefits of lineage-specific adaptation over model scaling alone. These improvements extended to all six tested algal species, increasing mean accuracy from 26.3% to 37.5%, although performance varied across ferns and gymnosperms. BryoCAD also enhanced gene structure annotation: replacing PlantCAD2-Small with BryoCAD-Small increased transcript-level F1 scores from 0.578 to 0.625 in  Marchantia polymorpha and from 0.485 to 0.530 in  Physcomitrium patens . Together, our findings demonstrate that lineage- specific continued pre-training enhances genomic sequence interpretation and gene annotation across bryophytes, providing a transferable framework for extending DNA foundation models to evolutionarily diverse, understudied plant lineages.

papers.abstract_full: Autoregressive DNA language models generate sequences efficiently from left to right, but many genome-analysis and sequence-editing problems are naturally conditioned on both flanks. We introduce  CreatiPhage , a 144.5M-parameter autoregressive DNA language model for bacteriophages, and its diffusion extension,  CreatiPhage Diffusion DNA-LM (CPDD) . CPDD is a 147.5M-parameter bidirectional discrete diffusion model initialized from the six-epoch CreatiPhage checkpoint. CPDD retains the pretrained Transformer, block attention residuals, and Engram conditional memory, while introducing non-causal attention, a MASK-aware base-5 Engram, centered depthwise convolution, and position-aligned nucleotide readout. Training combines masked and GIDD-style uniformly substituted bases with nucleotide- and amino-acid-level losses over a 10 kb, 32 kb, and whole-source context curriculum. On a screened panel of 522 phage CDSs, CPDD achieves higher random-mask restoration accuracy than a comparable diffusion model and performs well above codon-level references. In a mixed-corruption test, it restores 42.4% of visible incorrect bases. Frozen CPDD representations also support  infA fitness prediction and seven-class phage virion protein subtype classification. Controlled evaluations further characterize how restoration depends on visible context and identify opportunities to improve longer-range sequence recovery. Together, these results support scaffold-conditioned sequence modeling as a step towards modular design of phage genomes.

papers.abstract: Accurate and efficient EC number prediction is essential for elucidating enzyme function. papers.abstract_full: Accurate and efficient EC number prediction is essential for elucidating enzyme function. Although similarity-based and deep learning-based approaches have advanced this task, they often fail to distinguish active enzymes from sequence-similar decoys inactivated by functional-site mutations, resulting in high false-positive rates (FPRs). We propose DecoyOpt, a two-stage pipeline for decoy-aware enzyme discrimination and fourth-level EC number prediction. Specifically, putatively inactive functional-site decoys were generated using ESM3, and 16 protein language models were evaluated across three data splits. In the first stage, a multilayer perceptron trained with classification and ranking losses discriminates enzymes from unannotated proteins and decoys. Then, predicted enzymes are assigned EC numbers using a contrastive learning model. On the most stringent GraphPart 40% split, DecoyOpt achieves an MCC of 0.899 for enzyme discrimination and a D  0 decoy FPR of 6.17%, outperforming retrained baseline methods. Across all splits, DecoyOpt consistently surpasses these baselines in EC number prediction on the full test set while maintaining performance comparable to CLEAN on the enzyme-only subset. Furthermore, it correctly annotates all four wild-type enzymes and rejects all eight deleterious variants. These results suggest that DecoyOpt provides robust annotation for uncharacterized proteins and functional variants, with potential applications in genomics, synthetic biology, and biocatalysis.

papers.abstract_full: OBJECTIVE: To systematically map the internal 2'-O-methylation (Nm) landscape on messenger RNA (mRNA) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), characterize its distribution features and biological functions, and identify key C/D box small nucleolar RNAs (snoRNAs) that regulate Nm modification along with their target genes, thereby providing a molecular basis for elucidating post-transcriptional regulatory mechanisms in HCC. METHODS: Based on Nanopore direct RNA sequencing data from the HepG2 cell line, we employed the NanoNm machine learning algorithm to systematically identify internal Nm modification sites on mRNA and analyzed their sequence preferences, genomic distribution, and methylation ratio characteristics. Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses were then performed to explore the biological functions of the modified genes. Using snoRNA expression profiles from the GSE233521 dataset derived from liver cancer stem cells, we conducted differential expression analysis to screen for significantly differentially expressed C/D box snoRNAs. Based on the principle of sequence complementarity, we predicted their guided Nm-modified target genes. Subsequently, hepatocellular carcinoma single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data were used to characterize the cell-type-specific expression of the target genes. RESULTS: A total of 10,450 high-confidence consensus Nm modification sites were identified, spanning 1515 genes. These modification sites exhibited a significant sequence preference for AGmA and UCmU trinucleotide motifs (where "m" denotes 2'-O-methylation). Genes bearing Nm modifications were significantly enriched in pathways associated with energy metabolism and protein synthesis, including oxidative phosphorylation, ribosome assembly, and cytoplasmic translation. SNORD88B was significantly upregulated in liver cancer stem cells, its guide sequence displayed perfect base-pairing complementarity with the Nm-modified region of fibronectin 1 (FN1) mRNA. Furthermore, single-cell RNA sequencing analysis revealed that FN1 was specifically expressed in hepatocellular carcinoma tumor cell clusters. CONCLUSION: This study systematically mapped the global landscape of internal Nm modifications on HCC mRNA at single-base resolution. Nm modification may participate in the development and progression of HCC by modulating the expression and function of target genes. The high expression of SNORD88B in liver cancer stem cells may promote the malignant progression of HCC by guiding Nm modification on FN1 mRNA, thereby providing new research directions for an in-depth understanding of the regulatory mechanisms of snoRNA-mediated Nm modification in HCC.
