selected_papers.abstract_full: Alzheimer's disease (AD) exhibits high clinical and biological heterogeneity, which complicates the development of one-size-fits-all therapeutic strategies. Standard trial designs can mask subgroup-specific effects, highlighting the need to move towards precision neurology entailing multisystem genomics, biomarkers, and artificial intelligence (AI) integrative signals. The aim of the study is to critically synthesize and evaluate emerging strategies for drug optimization and individual therapeutic algorithms informed by genomic architecture, pharmacogenomics (PGx), and polygenic risk scores (PRS) with the opinion to resolve the controversy and unanswered question. Amplify the convergence into amyloid processing, lipid metabolism, and innate immunity seen from monogenic mutations and over 80 GWAS risk loci. Genotyping of CYP2D6 and CYP2C19 variants permits pharmacogenomic stratifications for the optimization of cholinesterase inhibitor and psychotropic dosing, thereby reducing adverse events. Variants of the alleles APOE ε4 and immune-related factors (e.g., FCGR3A) are significant in predicting the effects of ARIA associated with amyloid on anti-amyloid immunotherapy outcomes. PRS and deep phenotyping (including digital and fluid-based biomarkers) allow for the identification of unique biological endotypes (e.g., tau-dominant vs. vascular-inflammatory) that improve clinical trial enrichment and prognostication. This framework delineates molecular endotypes and translates CYP2D6 or APOE stratification into drug dosing and ARIA risk predictions. These biomarker-driven strategies shift AD management from a passive, reactive therapeutic scheme to an active, personalized one. Utilization of high-dimensional data streams via AI-driven learning health systems converts AD management from a reactive, symptom-based model to that which is proactive and hallmark biomarker-driven precision.

selected_papers.abstract_full: Multi-trait Polygenic Risk Score (mtPRS) methods improve prediction accuracy compared to single-trait PRS (stPRS) by integrating genetically correlated traits. Current mtPRS methods primarily use three approaches: (1) aggregating genome-wide association studies (GWAS) summary statistics; (2) combining individual PRSs with weights from Principal Component Analysis (PCA); or (3) combining individual PRSs with multivariate or penalized regression-derived weights. However, existing mtPRS methods face two main challenges: (1) selected variants are often non-causal, lowering prediction power; and (2) no method is universally superior across diverse genetic architectures and multi-trait correlation structures. To improve prediction performance and robustness, we propose mtPRS-FIMEL (multi-trait Polygenic Risk Score using FIne-Mapping and Ensemble Learning), an ensemble learning approach that integrates fine-mapping with multi-trait PRS construction. mtPRS-FIMEL computes mtPRS by combining multiple complementary mtPRS and stPRS methods and strategically leveraging causal variants identified through fine-mapping analysis. Specifically, it uses GWAS summary statistics to estimate causal effects and learn optimal weights for a set of PRSs from complementary mtPRS (including mtPRS-PCA, a PCA based method, and mtPRS-ML, an elastic-net based machine learning method, and stPRS). Our extensive simulations demonstrate that mtPRS-FIMEL outperforms existing mtPRS and stPRS methods in terms of prediction accuracy, PRS association strength, and patient stratification performance in the simulation settings examined. Validation with PGx GWAS data from a randomized clinical trial successfully predicted the drug response of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) change from baseline, while integrating three LDL-C-related traits (LDL, HDL, and Triglycerides) from disease GWAS, confirming its promising performance and robustness via a proof-of-concept internally cross-validated approach.

selected_papers.abstract_full: INTRODUCTION: Polygenic risk score (PRS) is a valuable tool for predicting the risk of breast cancer (BC). However, limited studies have been conducted in Chinese women. This study aimed to develop and validate a PRS which could be used to identify individuals with high risk of breast cancer. The associations between the PRS and patients' clinicopathological characteristics or survival outcomes were also evaluated. METHODS: We developed a PRS based on genome-wide association studies (GWAS)-identified risk variants with a three-stage design across four cohorts. In total, 7,056 patients and 6,659 controls were enrolled from Fujian Medical University Union Hospital (FJMUUH) and Shanghai Breast Cancer Genetics Study (SBCGS). Five approaches were utilized to calculate the PRS, including repeated logistic regression (RLR), logistic ridge regression (LRR), artificial neural network (ANN), random forest (RF) and support vector machine (SVM). Logistic regression analyses were performed to assess the association between established PRS and clinicopathological characteristics. The correlation between PRS and patients' survival outcomes was evaluated by Cox regression models. RESULTS: Overall, 7 SNPs were selected for PRS development. PRSLRR achieved robust and stable performance across cohorts, yielding an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.633 and an OR of 1.64 per 1 SD increase. Women in the top5% and 80-95% percentiles of PRS had a 4.32-fold and a 1.40-fold elevated risk of developing breast cancer compared with those at average risk (PRS in 40-60th percentiles). The predictive performance of PRS for patients with human epidermal growth factor receptor-2 (HER-2) positive tumors was demonstrated to be higher than that of HER-2 negative tumors (AUC = 0.671 vs. 0.623). It was also identified that the PRS was not correlated with age at diagnosis or tumor characteristics. In multivariable Cox models, high PRS was associated with worse overall survival (OS) in the overall cohort (adjusted HR = 1.39, 95%CI = 1.08-1.78, p = 0.010) and unfavorable disease-free survival (DFS) (adjusted HR = 1.41, 95%CI = 1.03-1.95; p = 0.035)/OS (adjusted HR = 1.64, 95%CI = 1.14-2.37, p = 0.008) in estrogen receptor (ER) negative patients. CONCLUSION: The PRS could provide additional information for Chinese women at high risk of breast cancer and holds significant value for BC screening. An increase in PRS also indicates an unfavorable prognosis and might play a crucial role in the clinical management of breast cancer patients at the time of diagnosis.

selected_papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Hypertension and type 2 diabetes (T2D) frequently coexist, but whether hypertension independently contributes to earlier diabetes onset beyond shared metabolic and genetic susceptibility remains incompletely understood. This study investigates the longitudinal relationship between hypertension and subsequent T2D risk using survival analysis and survival machine learning approaches. METHODS: A matched cohort analysis was conducted using UK Biobank participants free of diabetes at baseline, and a 6-month lag period was applied to reduce reverse causation. Time-to-event analyses were performed using Cox proportional hazards models. Genetic susceptibility was evaluated using both a genome-wide polygenic risk score (PRS) and a targeted multi-variant score (TMS). Survival machine learning models including XGBoost, Random Survival Forests, and ridge-penalized Cox regression were evalueted under identical train/test splits. Additional robustness analyses incorporated antihypertensive medication classes, genetic principal components, broader hypertension phenotype definitions integrating blood pressure measurements and medication use, stricter baseline diabetes exclusion criteria, extended lag-period analyses, and time-stratified sensitivity analyses. RESULTS: The final multivariable matched analytic cohort included 76,439 participants (37,951 individuals with HTN and 38,488 matched controls). During follow-up, 4,315 incident T2D events occurred, including 3,571 among individuals with HTN and 744 among controls. Hypertension remained independently associated with T2D after adjustment for adiposity, lipid traits, statin use, antihypertensive medication classes, genetic principal components, and genetic susceptibility (HR 1.30, p < 0.001). Individuals with hypertension developed T2D earlier, with reduced diabetes-free survival over follow-up. Both PRS and TMS independently predicted T2D risk and demonstrated significant interactions with hypertension. Survival machine learning analyses showed progressive improvement in discrimination following incorporation of hypertension and genetic susceptibility, with XGBoost demonstrating the highest performance (C-index 0.823, 95% CI 0.812-0.833). Importantly, the observed association remained robust across multiple sensitivity analyses, demonstrating persistence of the association beyond the early post-index period. CONCLUSIONS: Hypertension is associated with an increased and earlier T2D risk independent of metabolic risk factors and genetic susceptibility. Polygenic risk further stratifies diabetes risk but does not explain the relationship between hypertension and earlier T2D onset. The consistency of the findings across sensitivity analyses and survival-learning frameworks supports hypertension as an important component of the cardiometabolic trajectory preceding T2D development.

selected_papers.abstract_full: Background  Genomic studies in hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) are limited by sample sizes and targeted approaches. Methods  The Genomic Studies in Blood and Marrow Transplantation (GS-BMT) project is a collaboration between the National Cancer Institute (NCI) and the CIBMTR® designed to investigate recipient and donor determinants of HCT outcomes. We are generating genome-wide SNP-array genotyping for all samples, and sequencing and methylation profiling for selected subsets. We report study design and cohort characteristics and present two proof-of-concept analyses: comparison of conventional and machine learning prediction of overall survival after HCT in 9,262 patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML), and assessment of inherited susceptibility to clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) among 19,750 HCT donors using polygenic scores (PGS). Results  GS-BMT includes 30,718 donor–recipient pairs who received allogeneic HCT in the United States between 2000 and 2019. In AML, clinical variables alone provided modest prediction for post-transplant survival, with similar performance for Cox proportional hazards, random survival forest, and deep neural network survival models (C-index=0.63, 0.62, and 0.62, respectively). In donors, CHIP-PGS did not differ by age (p=0.76) but was modestly lower in unrelated  vs . related donors (−0.06 standard deviation [SD]; p=0.002). In an illustrative analysis assuming risk of event increases by 50% or 80% per PGS-SD, the top 5.2% and 12.3% of the donors, respectively, would have at least twice the risk of a donor with the average PGS.  Conclusions  GS-BMT establishes a large genomic platform aiming to improve individualized risk prediction, donor selection, and precision medicine in HCT.

selected_papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Three-dimensional fast spin-echo MR cisternography (CUBE) of the internal auditory canal (IAC) and cerebellopontine angle (CPA) requires longer acquisition times that can limit clinical throughput. We evaluated whether a deep learning (DL)-based highly accelerated reconstruction technique, Sonic DL`™ (SDL), combined with a commercially available DL denoising reconstruction (AIR™ Recon DL, ARDL), preserves or improves subjective image quality and cochlear anatomy visualization relative to standard CUBE-ARDL while shortening scan time. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Consecutive patients underwent brain MRI for suspected IAC pathology at 1.5T and 3T with paired acquisition of standard 3D CUBE-ARDL and an accelerated 3D CUBE-SDL sequence. Both used the same voxel size at 1.5T (0.6x0.6x1.2 mm3) and 3T (0.6x0.6x0.6 mm3). Scan times for CUBE-ARDL versus CUBE-SDL were 2:33 versus 1:41 min at 1.5T and 1:55 versus 1:11 min at 3T. Two independent neuroradiologists blinded to MRI acquisition method scored randomized, de-identified images on a 5-point Likert scale across five domains (overall image quality, noise, sharpness, artifacts, cochlear anatomy visualization). Reader-averaged scores for CUBE-ARDL and CUBE-SDL were compared with paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, with reader-specific and cumulative link mixed model (CLMM) sensitivity analyses and false discovery rate (FDR) adjustment; intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) quantified inter-reader reliability for each technique; Gwet's AC2 and weighted (Conger's) kappa with linear ordinal weights quantified pooled inter-reader agreement. RESULTS: After exclusion of 5 training cases per field strength, 49 (1.5T) and 34 (3T) patients were analyzed. CUBE-SDL scored significantly better than CUBE-ARDL for all five domains at both field strengths (all FDR-adjusted P < .001), consistently for each reader and in the CLMM. Inter-reader reliability (ICC) for CUBE-SDL was moderate-to-excellent at 3T (0.63-0.92) and moderate at 1.5T (0.65-0.74), generally exceeding CUBE-ARDL (3T: 0.35-0.61; 1.5T: 0.50-0.71). Pooled inter-reader agreement (Gwet's AC2) ranged from 0.56 to 0.89. CONCLUSIONS: A combined Sonic DL acceleration with ARDL-denoised reconstruction for 3D T2 CUBE produced significantly higher subjective image quality at both 1.5T and 3T, and, at 3T, higher inter-reader reliability than standard CUBE-ARDL, while shortening acquisition time by 34%-38%. These findings support further evaluation, including diagnostic accuracy studies, of CUBE-SDL as an alternative to CUBE-ARDL.

selected_papers.abstract_full: ABSTRACT  The mammillary bodies are a central component of the hippocampal–diencephalic-cingulate network that is critically involved in emotion processing and memory function, yet their genetic architecture remains unknown. We conducted a genome-wide association study (GWAS) of mammillary body volume in 38,064 participants from the UK Biobank and replicated our findings in the Rhineland Study cohort (N = 4,860). Mammillary body and hypothalamic subregional volumes were derived from structural brain MRIs using FastSurfer-HypVINN, an established and validated deep learning-based segmentation tool. Univariate GWAS identified 34 genomic loci associated with mammillary body volume, including 26 novel loci, with 20 loci showing replication in the Rhineland Study. Meta-analysis across both cohorts (N = 42,924) identified 44 associated loci, of which 35 were novel. Multivariate GWAS of hypothalamic subregions identified 55 loci, including 40 novel associations. Integrative cross-omics analyses identified  MEI1 and CAPZA1 as key molecular candidates, with genetically regulated  MEI1 expression and circulating CAPZA1 protein levels partially mediating genetic effects on mammillary body volume. Genetic correlation and Mendelian randomization analyses further revealed a bidirectional relationship between mammillary body volume and major depressive disorder. Together, our findings elucidate the genetic architecture of mammillary body volume and its relation to mental disorders.

selected_papers.abstract_full: Fatty acid composition is a major determinant of nutritional quality, oxidative stability and functional value of oilseed crops. It is shaped by coordinated plastidial fatty acid synthesis, endoplasmic reticulum-associated desaturation and elongation, acyl editing, triacylglycerol assembly and lipid turnover in seed. This review summarizes the metabolic basis of fatty acid diversity of edible oil in major and specialty oilseed crops, then examines how genetic architecture and omics-assisted discovery have accelerated the identification of loci, alleles and candidate genes controlling fatty acid composition. We emphasize a design framework that links locus discovery to allele prioritization, targeted editing, pathway engineering and field deployment. Linkage mapping, bulked segregant sequencing, genome wide association studies, transcriptomics, proteomics and pangenome analyses are increasingly revealing both canonical genes and previously unrecognized structural or regulatory variation. We further discuss improvement strategies ranging from conventional and marker-assisted breeding to single-gene editing, transgenic manipulation and multigene synthetic biology. Finally, we highlight emerging opportunities in population genomics, underutilized oil crop mining, artificial intelligence (AI)-guided enzyme and promoter design, and agronomic evaluation. Collectively, these advances are shifting oilseed improvement from empirical selection toward rational, pathway-informed design of fatty acid profiles, while emphasizing the continuing need for biochemical validation and field-level performance assessment.

selected_papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) has a heterogeneous genetic architecture in which risk-associated genes may participate in interconnected molecular pathways. We present an graph-explainable multi-view graph neural network (GEM-GNN) for prioritizing ASD-associated genes by integrating protein-protein interaction (PPI) and brain-specific co-expression networks with genomic features. The model uses two GraphSAGE branches to learn representations from the structural and functional network views, combines these representations through a feature bottleneck, and applies an adjusted focal-loss objective to address class imbalance. Permutation feature importance and neighborhood subgraph extraction are used to examine the genomic and network evidence underlying candidate rankings. In experiments covering 19,832 protein-coding genes, the manuscript reports an area under the precision-recall curve of 0.8008, an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.93, an F1 score of 0.74 and a precision at 100 of 76%. An ablation analysis reports an AUPRC of 0.80 for the bottleneck-fusion model, compared with 0.71 for the PPI-only model, 0.69 for the co-expression-only model and 0.75 for simple concatenation. The authors also report that 85 high-ranking candidates overlap with independent de novo mutation evidence and that candidate genes are enriched for RNA polymerase II-mediated transcriptional processes. These results suggest that combining structural and brain-specific functional networks may support ASD gene prioritization and pathway-level interpretation. The reported performance and biological findings require interpretation in light of the dataset construction, evaluation protocol and validation procedures described in the manuscript.

selected_papers.abstract_full: AIMS: Ketone bodies are implicated in cardiovascular metabolism, yet the contributions of β-hydroxybutyrate (BHB), acetoacetate and acetone to coronary atherosclerosis remain unclear. METHODS: We integrated Mendelian randomization (MR), cross-trait GWAS analysis, ApoE pQTL-MR and colocalization to investigate genetic associations with coronary atherosclerosis, complemented by bulk transcriptomic analysis, machine learning-based signature construction, immune infiltration analysis and single-cell analysis to characterize APOE-associated molecular features in human atherosclerotic plaques. RESULTS: Genetically predicted BHB was associated with coronary atherosclerosis risk in univariable MR (OR = 1.59, 95% CI: 1.29-1.95, p = 8.8 × 10-6) and remained significant after mutual adjustment for acetoacetate and acetone (OR = 1.58, 95% CI: 1.14-2.18, p = 0.005), whereas neither acetoacetate nor acetone showed a significant association. Cross-trait gene prioritization highlighted APOE for further investigation. ApoE pQTL-MR supported an association between genetically predicted ApoE and coronary atherosclerosis (OR = 1.23, p = 0.003). Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) and machine-learning algorithms, including LASSO, random forest, SVM-RFE and XGBoost, identified an APOE-associated five-gene signature comprising XAF1, CEP128, TMEM106A, VEPH1 and ABCB1. The signature achieved an apparent AUC of 0.956 in GSE43292 and AUCs of 0.974 in GSE100927 and 0.736 in GSE28829. High signature scores were associated with immune-inflammatory changes. Single-cell analysis showed enrichment of the signature in macrophages, endothelial cells and fibroblasts, while CellChat analysis identified a macrophage-centred pattern of inferred cell-cell communication. CONCLUSIONS: These findings identify BHB as the ketone body most strongly associated with coronary atherosclerosis susceptibility and define an APOE-associated multicellular signature in human atherosclerotic plaques with potential value for molecular stratification.

selected_papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) is a genetic disorder impairing mucociliary clearance. This study provides a comprehensive analysis of clinical and genetic characteristics in a large Turkish cohort with frequent parental consanguinity. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was performed on 145 patients (selected from 361) with regular follow-up since 2017 to ensure longitudinal data consistency. The diagnostic work-up included nasal nitric oxide measurement and high-speed videomicroscopy, while confirmation was established through genetic testing and/or transmission electron microscopy. Patients were classified according to the 2025 ATS/ERS diagnostic framework. Patients were evaluated for clinical predictors, longitudinal pulmonary function, and genotype-phenotype correlations based on structural protein localization. RESULTS: Among 145 patients (mean age 15.91 ± 6.26 years), early diagnosis was significantly associated with neonatal respiratory distress syndrome (p = 0.014), NICU admission (p < 0.001), situs inversus totalis (p < 0.001), and congenital heart disease (p < 0.001). The mean PICADAR score was 7.8 ± 3.4, showing a moderate negative correlation with age at diagnosis (r = -0.50, p < 0.001). According to the 2025 ATS/ERS diagnostic framework, 63 patients (43.4%) were classified as confirmed PCD, 13 (9.0%) as PCD highly likely, and 69 (47.6%) as suspected PCD. Among confirmed PCD patients, the most frequent genetic findings were DNAH5, CCDC40, and DNAAF1. Lower final FEV1 values were observed in selected rare genotype subgroups, particularly CCNO, although variant-specific comparisons were limited by small subgroup sizes. CONCLUSION: Early recognition of neonatal respiratory distress requiring NICU admission and laterality defects, particularly situs inversus totalis, remains critical for reducing diagnostic delay. In populations with high consanguinity, genetic testing is particularly important for confirming diagnosis and identifying potentially high-risk genotypes. Multidisciplinary follow-up focusing on nutrition, infection control, and preservation of lung function is essential for long-term care in PCD.

selected_papers.abstract_full: INTRODUCTION: Situs inversus is a rare congenital condition characterized by a mirror-image reversal of thoracic and/or abdominal organs, with an estimated incidence of 1 in 10,000 live births. Although many individuals are asymptomatic, the condition is associated with congenital heart disease (CHD), and because a mirror-image heart may appear structurally normal, it can be overlooked at routine prenatal ultrasonography unless fetal laterality is determined first. CASE DESCRIPTION: A 25-year-old primigravida was referred at 34-35 weeks of gestation for evaluation of fetal growth restriction; fetal situs inversus had not been identified at previous antenatal examinations. Ultrasonography showed the stomach on the right, the liver on the left, the descending aorta to the right of the spine and the inferior vena cava to the left, with the cardiac apex directed to the right. Fetal echocardiography confirmed atrial situs inversus with mirror-image dextrocardia and normal systemic and pulmonary venous return, without structural cardiac defects or features of heterotaxy. Doppler indices were normal, and the fetus was categorized as small for gestational age. The patient delivered a neonate weighing 2365 grams vaginally at 39 weeks and 4 days, and postnatal echocardiography confirmed mirror-image dextrocardia with normal intracardiac anatomy. CONCLUSION: Isolated situs inversus totalis can remain undetected until the third trimester because each standard view of a mirror-image heart appears normal. selected_papers.abstract_full: Ellis-Yale-Winter syndrome (EYWS) is an exceptionally rare multiple congenital anomaly syndrome characterized by microcephaly and congenital heart disease, variably associated with unilateral renal agenesis and abnormal pulmonary lobation. Its phenotype derives from a single original sibship, no validated diagnostic criteria exist, and no causative gene has been established. We report a male infant with congenital microcephaly, right renal agenesis with a contralateral ectopic solitary kidney, congenital heart defects, craniofacial dysmorphic features, and neurological abnormalities. The findings showed phenotypic overlap with the original cases, leading a multidisciplinary team to a suspected clinical diagnosis of EYWS. This diagnosis is not molecularly confirmed, as no genetic testing was performed. Pulmonary lobation and segmentation could not be assessed, which is a major limitation; their presence or absence cannot be inferred. The contralateral renal ectopia may represent a coincidental malformation or a hypothetical phenotypic variant. Long-term outcome and vital status are undetermined. This report does not establish new diagnostic features or an expanded phenotypic spectrum. Dedicated pulmonary imaging, exome or genome sequencing, DNA banking, and longitudinal follow-up are recommended in future cases.

selected_papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Coffin-Lowry syndrome is a rare X-linked genetic disorder caused by pathogenic variants in the RPS6KA3 gene, characterized by distinctive craniofacial features, skeletal abnormalities, and neurodevelopmental impairment. Although cardiac involvement has been reported in Coffin-Lowry syndrome, it most commonly manifests as cardiomyopathy or valvular insufficiency. To the best of our knowledge, Coffin-Lowry syndrome has not been associated with obstructive left-sided congenital heart diseases including an incomplete Shone's complex. CASE PRESENTATION: We report a case of a 2-month-old boy who, on cardiac evaluation, was found to have coarctation of the aorta, a bicuspid aortic valve with severe stenosis, a parachute-like mitral valve with mild subvalvular stenosis, consistent with an incomplete Shone's complex, and marked left ventricular hypertrophy. The patient underwent successful corrective surgery for coarctation of the aorta and aortic valve stenosis, with follow-up revealing moderate residual aortic valve stenosis and mild residual valvular dysfunction. Genetic testing identified a maternally inherited microduplication of the X chromosome p22.12 region, encompassing several 5' exons of the RPS6KA3 gene. CONCLUSIONS: This case suggests that obstructive left-sided congenital heart diseases including an incomplete Shone's complex may represent a previously unrecognized cardiac manifestations of Coffin-Lowry syndrome, thereby expanding the cardiovascular phenotype of this rare condition. Recognition of this association may have implications for early diagnosis, genetic evaluation, and long-term cardiac surveillance in affected patients.

selected_papers.abstract_full: INTRODUCTION: Ring chromosome 21 (r (21)) is a rare constitutional rearrangement involving terminal deletions and significant phenotypic heterogeneity. High-resolution genomic analyses have demonstrated that ring chromosomes may harbor complex genomic imbalances and dynamic mosaicism. However, the contributions of ring chromosome instability, tissue-specific mosaicism, and complex dosage imbalance to the clinical phenotype remain poorly understood. CASE PRESENTATION: We report an 8-month-old boy with developmental delay, congenital heart disease, hearing impairment, structural brain abnormalities, and dysmorphic features suggestive of Down syndrome (DS), although lacking the complete classical phenotype. Cytogenomic analyses identified a constitutional non-supernumerary r (21) associated with a 18.77-Mb duplication of 21q21.2-q22.3 and a 3.09-Mb terminal deletion of 21q22.3. Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) resolved the ring chromosome structure, identifying four instability-derived clones, and demonstrated tissue-specific mosaicism across lymphocytes, oral mucosa epithelial cells, and urinary sediment epithelial cells, with a duplicated monocentric r (21) as the predominant clone. Comparison with the four previously reported constitutional non-supernumerary r (21) cases revealed a recurrent combination of Down syndrome critical region (DSCR) duplication and terminal 21q deletion, despite substantial phenotypic variability. DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION: This study expands the clinical and cytogenomic spectrum associated with constitutional non-supernumerary r (21). Tissue-specific mosaicism and recurrent genomic imbalances suggest that the DS-like phenotype cannot be explained solely by dosage alterations involving the classical or highly restricted DSCR. Our findings suggest a mechanism in which dynamic ring chromosome instability, and the cumulative dosage imbalance of multiple chromos​ome 21 genes, contribute to the phenotypic variability observed in these patients. Additional well-characterized cases are essential for refining the genotype-phenotype correlations of this rare genomic disorder.

selected_papers.abstract_full: Accurate assessment of patient knowledge is an essential component of informed decision-making in cardiac genetic testing. An eight-item cardiac genetic knowledge scale was previously developed to support evaluation of informed choice within the Multidimensional Model of Informed Choice, but its psychometric properties have not been formally assessed. Data were pooled from 318 adults with hypertrophic or dilated cardiomyopathy who received pretest education through a genetics webinar (n = 121), cardiologist-led counseling (n = 61), or a prerecorded educational video (n = 136). Exploratory factor analysis (EFA), confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), and two-parameter logistic item response theory (IRT) modeling were used to evaluate factor structure, item performance, and measurement precision. Mean knowledge scores ranged from 6.2 to 7.1 out of 8, with 62%-91% of participants classified as having adequate knowledge (≥ 75%). EFA supported a two-factor solution reflecting disease-related and testing-related knowledge; however, CFA demonstrated substantial overlap between these domains (r = 0.81), with one- and two-factor models showing comparable fit. Overall, findings supported a dominant general knowledge construct. IRT analyses demonstrated acceptable model fit (M2 = 39.35, df = 20, p = 0.006) and meaningful variability in item performance. Two items showed strong discrimination across the knowledge continuum, while several items contributed less information. All items had negative difficulty parameters, indicating that the scale was primarily targeted toward individuals with below-average knowledge. Test information curves showed greatest measurement precision at low-to-moderate knowledge levels. Raw scores were highly correlated with latent trait estimates (r = 0.97, p < 0.001), supporting the practicality of simple sum-score interpretation. This study provides preliminary evidence supporting the internal structural validity of the eight-item cardiac genetic knowledge scale. The scale demonstrated acceptable item performance in this sample and effectively identified individuals with lower levels of knowledge and specific educational gaps across care models, supporting its potential use as the knowledge component of informed decision-making measures in cardiac genetic testing.

selected_papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: MYBPC3 truncating variants (MYBPC3tv) represent the most common genetic substrate in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, yet carriers show substantial phenotypic variability despite a shared mechanism of haploinsufficiency. The contribution of additional genetic variants to this variability remains incompletely defined. METHODS: We analyzed 11 991 unrelated hypertrophic cardiomyopathy probands undergoing clinical genetic testing. Analyses focused on MYBPC3tv carriers stratified by additional intermediate-effect variants (IEVs) or second monogenic variants. IEVs were further classified as sarcomeric or nonsarcomeric. All probands were genetically characterized at a single center using standardized sequencing protocols, with uniform ascertainment of IEVs throughout the study period. Primary outcomes included age-related penetrance, maximal left ventricular wall thickness, and major adverse cardiovascular events; independent predictors were assessed by a multivariable Cox regression model. RESULTS: Among 2767 genotype-positive probands, MYBPC3 accounted for 47.6% of cases, with truncating variants representing 81.9% of MYBPC3-positive individuals. Within MYBPC3tv carriers, additional variants were associated with a stepwise gradient of disease severity. Median age at diagnosis decreased from 48 years in isolated carriers to 42 years in MYBPC3tv+IEV and 28 years in double-monogenic carriers, whereas mean wall thickness increased from 21.3 to 24.1 and 26.3 mm, respectively. In multivariable analyses, cumulative genetic burden remained an independent predictor of major adverse cardiovascular event. Sarcomeric IEV carriers (hazard ratio, 10.3 [95% CI, 2.3-28.7]) and biallelic MYBPC3 carriers (hazard ratio, 23.2 [95% CI, 5.3-115.0]) exhibited the highest risk, although estimates in these subgroups should be interpreted cautiously given the limited number of events. All biallelic MYBPC3 carriers were diagnosed in childhood. CONCLUSIONS: Cumulative rare variant burden explains a subset of the phenotypic heterogeneity among MYBPC3tv carriers, defining a hierarchical gradient of disease expression. Intermediate-effect alleles and second monogenic variants, particularly biallelic MYBPC3, identify higher-risk subgroups that may benefit from intensified surveillance, individualized management, and guided therapies.
